dimensions.notes:
Overall (scope: HandProto root and HandProto/Input, following calls into Core):
- I found no per-frame string concat/format/ToString, LINQ, lambdas/closures, Enum.HasFlag or dictionary-with-enum boxing, per-frame Debug.Log, per-frame TMP text writes, or non-NonAlloc physics in the scoped files. PointingBeamController uses Physics.RaycastNonAlloc with a static 16-slot buffer, and ShockwaveController uses OverlapSphereNonAlloc with a static 32-slot buffer.
- Every Core function on the hot path is allocation-free: ChargeInputRule, ChargeShotModel.Step, ShotCooldown, AimAssist.SelectByAngle/SelectByRadius (they index an IReadOnlyList and never foreach it), AimCursorModel, ClutchMapper, SpringFlightModel/ArenaBounds, HeroHealthModel.Tick, BotBrain.Step, HandClutchSampler, PinchTrigger, TriggerGesture, PalmPush/PalmsTogether recognizers and HysteresisGate. All of them use structs and fields. HeroStats.From uses foreach over IReadOnlyList and boxes enumerators, but it runs only when the inventory's TotalLevels changes (per item pick), so it is not a hot path. RunHeroStats.StatsOf is called about 2-4 times per hero per frame (HeroHealth.Update twice via SyncMaxHealth and CurrentParams, plus FlyingCharacter and PointingBeamController); each call copies a 72-byte struct with no heap allocation, which is negligible.
- Steady-state managed allocation from this dimension is only GC-1: about 48 B x (1 player + N controlled bots) per frame, roughly 10-20 KB/s at 72-90 Hz. With incremental GC on, that alone is unlikely to explain multi-hundred-ms freezes. The spiky costs are per-event: GC-3 (Instantiate/Destroy per hit) and GC-4 (4 material clones per bot spawn, never freed; spawns also Instantiate a whole RunBot prefab in RunDirector, out of my scope). For a random freeze not tied to an island, the more likely sources are outside this dimension: RunDirector Instantiate/Destroy of bots and its per-spawn lambda `bot.Health.Died += () => OnBotDied(bot)`, HUD/menu TMP updates in Match/, Debug.Log volume elsewhere with usePlayerLog = 1, first-use shader/PSO creation for the impact or bot materials (Vulkan), and device-level causes such as thermal throttling or loss of input focus. The PerfSpikeLogger should record GC.CollectionCount(0) deltas to confirm or rule out GC.
- Non-findings, checked: DebugKeyboardMouseInputSource is added only when xr == false (Sandbox scene, HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:176-181), so it is not in the Arena_Main APK. HandPuppeteerController.clutchIndicator (`.material.color` at lines 82/90) is never assigned by the builder (line 185 sets only character and inputSource), so that path is dead in built scenes. BotTelegraphLine.LateUpdate writes positions, widths and colors every frame while telegraphing, but allocates nothing and needs those writes. XRHandsInputSource and HandGestureTracker.UpdateHand (foreach over a static array, XRHand.GetJoint structs) allocate nothing. The Quick Match bot's controllers on the "Bot" GameObject keep ticking while its hero is hidden during RUN, but with a disabled BotInputSource (Current = default, HasAim = false) they skip UpdateAim and allocate nothing. GetComponentInParent<PrototypeTarget>/<BeamHitReceiver> in Fire (lines 363/366) and GetComponentInParent<HeroHealth> in ShockwaveController.Fire (line 96) run per hit or per shockwave, not per frame; they are hierarchy walks with no allocation in player builds and are acceptable, though they could be cached per collider if desired.
- Event subscriptions (`health.Respawned += ResetAim` in PointingBeamController.OnEnable, `hitReceiver.Hit += OnHit` in BotInputSource.OnEnable) allocate a delegate on each enable. That happens per enable/disable toggle (pause, phase change), not per frame, so it is negligible.

findings.title: foreach over IReadOnlyList boxes the List enumerator every frame (CollectCandidates); for bots the whole scan is wasted
findings.frequency: per-frame, once per PointingBeamController that is aiming. Covers the player in ASSIST while the right hand is tracked (UpdateAim, line 253), the player every frame in CURSOR (UpdateCursor, line 289), and every controlled run bot while it perceives the player (bot input has HasAim = true).
findings.detail: AimAssistTarget.All is declared as IReadOnlyList<AimAssistTarget> (AimAssistTarget.cs:13). A foreach over that interface type calls IEnumerable<T>.GetEnumerator(), which boxes List<T>.Enumerator onto the heap (about 40-48 bytes on IL2CPP ARM64). This is the only steady per-frame managed allocation in this dimension, and it grows with bot count: about (1 + bots) x 72-90 Hz allocations per second. For bots the scan does nothing useful. The builder sets assistAngle = 0 on every bot PointingBeamController (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:664), so AimAssist.Cone yields acquire = 0 and AimAssist.SelectByAngle returns -1 before reading the list (AimAssist.cs:21, with current = -1 because a bot never has an _assistTarget). Each bot therefore pays for the allocation plus IsTargetable / IsChildOf / transform.position native calls every frame and gets nothing back.
findings.fix: Iterate by index: `var all = AimAssistTarget.All; for (int i = 0; i < all.Count; i++) { var t = all[i]; ... }`. Alternatively, expose the registry as `List<AimAssistTarget>` internally, or add a static `Count`/indexer accessor. Also skip CollectCandidates entirely when the acquire cone is 0 and no target is held: in UpdateAim, compute Cone() first and `if (acquire <= 0f && _assistTarget == null)` skip collection and SelectByAngle.
findings.vnote: Code is at PointingBeamController.cs:324, and AimAssistTarget.All is declared as IReadOnlyList<AimAssistTarget> (AimAssistTarget.cs:13). A foreach over the interface type calls IEnumerable<T>.GetEnumerator(), which boxes List<T>.Enumerator: one heap object of about 40-48 B per call under IL2CPP. I traced every caller. UpdateCursor runs every frame in CURSOR mode, gated only on source != null, so it also runs while XRHandsInputSource is disabled in menus, pauses and choice panels. UpdateAim runs every frame in ASSIST while HasAim is true. Bots set HasAim = true whenever they perceive the player (BotBrain.cs:180). The builder sets assistAngle = 0 on bots (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:664). AimAssist.Cone then gives acquire = 0, SelectByAngle returns -1 at AimAssist.cs:21 because current is always -1, and the bot scan is wasted, as the finder says. One correction: run bots are capped at RunParams.MaxAlive = 2 (RunStateMachine.cs:50/93), and the Quick Match bot's input is disabled during RUN (MatchDirector.cs:241). So the worst case is 3 controllers x 72-90 Hz x ~48 B, about 10-13 KB/s. That is the only steady per-frame managed allocation in HandProto and worth removing, but at that rate it cannot cause a freeze on its own with incremental GC. I rate it low, not medium.

findings.title: Hand-subsystem lookup allocates a List, strings, a string.Join and boxed bools every frame while no XRHandSubsystem is running
findings.frequency: per-frame, but only while `_subsystem == null || !_subsystem.running` (Update line 88-90): at startup, and on any frame where OpenXR has the hand subsystem stopped. The Debug.Log at line 141 fires only when the report text changes.
findings.detail: FindSubsystem() is called from Update every frame until a running subsystem is found. Each call allocates a new List<XRHandSubsystem>. When subsystems exist, ReportSubsystems also allocates a new List<string>, one interpolated string per subsystem, and the joined report string. The interpolation compiles to string.Format(string, object, object) under Unity's C# 9, which boxes the bool `s.running`. All of this happens only so it can be compared with _lastSubsystemReport. The cost is not paid during normal play, when the subsystem stays running. Whether Unity OpenXR stops the hand subsystem on Quest focus loss (system menu, boundary) is unverified, so how often this branch runs on device is uncertain. When the text changes, Debug.Log runs with ScriptOnly stack traces and usePlayerLog = 1, which is a costly call on Android, though rare.
findings.fix: Keep a cached `readonly List<XRHandSubsystem> _subsystems` and Clear() it. Throttle the search to about once per 0.5 s when it fails. Build the diagnostic string only when the count or running flags change (compare an int/bool signature first), and wrap the log in `[System.Diagnostics.Conditional("DEVELOPMENT_BUILD"), Conditional("UNITY_EDITOR")]` or `if (Debug.isDebugBuild)`.
findings.vnote: Code is at HandGestureTracker.cs:110-141. Update (line 88-90) calls FindSubsystem every frame while _subsystem is null or not running. While no subsystem exists, the report is a literal string and the only garbage is the new List. While subsystems exist but are stopped, it also allocates List<string>, the interpolated strings (string.Format boxing the bool under C# 9) and the joined string. Debug.Log fires only when the text changes. During normal play the subsystem stays running; losing hand tracking only sets XRHand.isTracked to false. Whether OpenXR stops the subsystem on device focus or session changes is unverified, and those moments are paused anyway (pauseOnFocusLoss). Accurate as stated, but not a credible cause of an in-play freeze.

findings.title: Hit effect is Instantiate'd and Destroy'ed on every beam hit (player and every bot)
findings.code:
GameObject fx = Instantiate(hitEffectPrefab, end, Quaternion.LookRotation(-dir));
Destroy(fx, 1f);
findings.frequency: per-hit: every shot whose ray from the hero to the aim point hits any collider (aimMask = -1, so floor, back wall, pillars, practice cubes and heroes all count). Covers player shots (cooldown 0.35 s, plus buffered and charge shots) and every run bot shot.
findings.detail: Each hit creates a new GameObject with a Transform, MeshFilter, MeshRenderer and ImpactFlash from the BeamImpact prefab (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:726-734), and destroys it 1 s later. That means native object creation and destruction, new managed wrappers, and garbage on every hit, from several shooters at once during an island. ImpactFlash already deactivates itself after 0.25 s (ImpactFlash.cs:22-25) and resets in OnEnable (lines 13-17), so the object sits inactive for about 0.75 s before Destroy and is already shaped for pooling. All bot PointingBeamControllers share the same prefab, so a shared pool is natural.
findings.fix: Add a small static pool, e.g. an ImpactFlashPool with a Stack<ImpactFlash> pre-warmed with about 8 instances at scene load, parented to a scene-level root and never to a bot, because run bots are Destroy'ed. Fire() takes an instance (or grows the pool), sets position and rotation, and calls SetActive(true). ImpactFlash returns itself to the pool instead of only calling SetActive(false). Remove Destroy(fx, 1f). Pre-warming also moves any first-use shader/PSO cost for the impact material to load time.
findings.vnote: Code is at PointingBeamController.cs:372-373 inside Fire(), which runs per shot. It spawns only if RaycastIgnoringSelf hits within dist + 0.5. aimMask = -1 and the aim point usually lies on a collider surface, so nearly every player shot spawns one. A bot shot spawns one when the ray reaches the player's 0.9 m sphere or any geometry. The prefab is a single sphere with MeshRenderer, MeshFilter and ImpactFlash (builder 726-734). ImpactFlash disables itself at 0.25 s and resets in OnEnable (ImpactFlash.cs:13-25), so it is ready for pooling. Rate: at most 2 bots (FireInterval 2.2 s + jitter) plus the player's 0.35 s cooldown, a few instantiates per second. Each Instantiate of a one-renderer prefab is tens of microseconds plus a few small managed wrappers. This is real churn and the pooling the user asked for, but not a freeze-scale cost. The finder's shader/PSO prewarm benefit is speculative: BeamImpact uses the same URP Unlit shader as the reticle and health bar, which are already rendered.

findings.title: renderer.material instancing in HeroHealth.Awake clones 4 materials per spawned run bot and never frees them
findings.frequency: per-spawn: every RunBot Instantiate (RunDirector.cs:192 spawns per island and again after each kill, gated by respawnInterval), plus once for the player hero. Later color writes (lines 245 and 252) happen per hit, per hit-flash end and per stun change.
findings.detail: Reading `r.material` clones the shared material for each hero renderer: Body, Nose, Fin_L and Fin_R on a bot, with the health bar excluded by IsChildOf. Unity does not destroy material instances created through Renderer.material when the GameObject is destroyed. Only Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets or a scene load frees them. No script calls UnloadUnusedAssets or LoadScene (grep), so every bot killed or despawned during a run (Destroy at RunDirector.cs:204/257) leaks 4 Material objects for the rest of the app session, across runs. The clones also add native work in the spawn frame (material creation, SRP Batcher constant-buffer setup) on top of the prefab Instantiate. GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>() and <Renderer>() in Awake also allocate arrays per spawn. The later `r.material.color = ...` writes in SetColor/RestoreColors reuse the existing instance and do not clone again.
findings.fix: Tint with a MaterialPropertyBlock instead: cache one MPB, use `Shader.PropertyToID("_BaseColor")` for URP Lit, and call renderer.GetPropertyBlock / SetPropertyBlock in SetColor; to restore, clear the block or set the base color read from sharedMaterial. MPB opts these renderers out of the SRP Batcher, which is fine for 4-5 renderers. If material instances must stay, store them in Awake and Destroy them in OnDestroy. Use `r.sharedMaterial.color` to read the base colors.
findings.vnote: HeroHealth.cs:81 reads r.material in Awake for Body, Nose, Fin_L and Fin_R. HealthBar is skipped by IsChildOf, and the ground marker sits outside the hero. That makes 4 Material clones per RunBot Instantiate (RunDirector.cs:192). Unity does not destroy Renderer.material instances when the object is destroyed; only Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets or a scene load frees them. I grepped: neither is called by game code. LoadScene appears only in legacy root scripts, and I checked by GUID that Arena_Main does not reference them. So the native-side leak is real and lasts the whole session. The managed wrappers are collected, so it does not grow the Boehm heap. Size: about 4 materials per bot, tens of bots per run (Horde respawns), so a few MB at most per session. The extra cost on the spawn frame is small. It is a real leak and should be fixed with an MPB or sharedMaterial, but it is not a freeze cause, so impact is low. The later r.material.color writes reuse the existing instance, as the finder says.

findings.title: SetVisible allocates a new Renderer[] via GetComponentsInChildren on every death and respawn
findings.code: foreach (Renderer r in GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true)) r.enabled = visible;
findings.frequency: per-event: Die() (each hero death) and Respawn(). Respawn also runs from ResetHealth / SetHealthScale (run bot setup and round start) and Revive.
findings.detail: Each call allocates a fresh Renderer[] (5 entries per hero) and walks the hierarchy. The collider array is already cached (_colliders, Awake line 74), but the renderer array is not. This is small garbage per event, not per frame. It adds to the spawn and death frames, which already carry Instantiate and Destroy work.
findings.fix: Cache `_allRenderers = GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true)` in Awake next to _colliders and loop that array with a for loop.
findings.vnote: HeroHealth.cs:239 allocates a Renderer[] from GetComponentsInChildren(true) on every SetVisible. That runs per event: Die, and Respawn via model Tick, ResetHealth, SetHealthScale at each bot spawn, and Revive. That is a few small arrays per death or spawn. Caching it next to _colliders is trivial.

findings.title: LockOnRing rewrites all 48 line points, colors and enabled state every frame, and calls Camera.main per frame
findings.frequency: per-frame (LateUpdate) while the player's aim is locked on a target, ASSIST or CURSOR.
findings.detail: This allocates nothing; it is per-frame waste. The ring is in local space (useWorldSpace = false) and only the scalar radius changes, yet each frame makes 48 separate SetPosition native calls with 48 Cos/Sin, sets startColor/endColor (line 79), which never change after Awake, and sets enabled = true (line 80). Camera.main (line 57) is a native lookup each frame; it is cheap in Unity 2020.2+ but avoidable.
findings.fix: Precompute a static unit-circle Vector3[48] once. Each frame either fill a cached Vector3[48] scaled by radius and call `line.SetPositions(cache)` once, or skip rewriting when radius has not changed beyond epsilon (it is constant once the pop settles and the distance is stable). Remove the per-frame color writes and only set enabled when it is false. Cache the head camera transform, e.g. HandGestureTracker's headCamera or a field set in Awake.
findings.vnote: LockOnRing.cs:55-80. LateUpdate makes 48 SetPosition calls with Cos/Sin, rewrites startColor/endColor and sets enabled = true every frame while a lock target exists. The lock exists only when the player's aim snapped: within 4 degrees in ASSIST, or within 1.2 m in CURSOR. Camera.main (line 57) is cached internally in modern Unity. Nothing here allocates; it is minor CPU waste, and a single SetPositions call from a cached array is the cleaner fix.

findings.title: Shockwave ring rebuilds 48 points with individual SetPosition calls and re-reads run stats every frame while visible
findings.frequency: per-frame for ringDuration (0.35 s) after each shockwave (player only; bots have no ShockwaveController).
findings.detail: There is no allocation. Each frame makes 48 native SetPosition calls plus trig, and `Radius` (line 121) calls RunHeroStats.StatsOf, which copies a 72-byte HeroStats struct each frame. The window is short and infrequent, so the impact is small.
findings.fix: Precompute unit-circle cos/sin once, fill a cached Vector3[ringSegments] and call ring.SetPositions(cache) once per frame. Compute the radius once in Fire() and store it for the ring animation.
findings.vnote: ShockwaveController.cs:120-130. For 0.35 s after each shockwave (3 s cooldown, player only; bots have no ShockwaveController), each frame makes 48 SetPosition calls. Radius calls RunHeroStats.StatsOf, which returns a cached 72-byte struct. RunHeroStats only recomputes when TotalLevels changes (RunHeroStats.cs:23), so nothing allocates. Negligible.

findings.title: HeroGroundMarker re-applies SetActive / enabled / positionCount every frame even when unchanged
findings.frequency: per-frame (LateUpdate) on every ground marker: the player hero, the CURSOR aim marker, each run bot, and the hidden Quick Match bot's marker if active.
findings.detail: This allocates nothing. Each frame makes redundant native calls: `.gameObject` plus SetActive with the same value, Renderer.enabled with the same value, and positionCount = 2 (line 46) although it never changes. Each is cheap, but they repeat for every marker, every frame.
findings.fix: Cache the last `visible` value and only call SetActive / enabled on change. Set positionCount = 2 once in Awake.
findings.vnote: HeroGroundMarker.cs:28-29 and 46 run every LateUpdate. Active markers are the player, at most 2 run bots, and the cursor marker only in CURSOR mode, because its GameObject is in cursorOnlyVisuals and is inactive in ASSIST. During RUN the Quick Match bot marker is inactive (hideDuringRun), so it never runs. GameObject.SetActive and Renderer.enabled with an unchanged value are near no-ops natively. Real redundancy, negligible cost.

findings.title: PointingBeamController calls Camera.main twice per frame and SetActive on the charge orb every frame
findings.code: float dist = Vector3.Distance(Camera.main != null ? Camera.main.transform.position : ray.origin, _rawAimPoint);
findings.frequency: per-frame for the player controller (reticle assigned; bots have no reticle). UpdateChargeIndicator (line 240, `chargeIndicator.gameObject.SetActive(step.Charging)`) also runs every frame for the player.
findings.detail: This allocates nothing. Camera.main is looked up twice per frame; it is cheap since Unity 2020.2 but still two native calls. The charge orb's SetActive is called every frame even when the state has not changed.
findings.fix: Cache the head camera Transform once (Awake, or via HandGestureTracker.headCamera). In UpdateChargeIndicator, only call SetActive when `chargeIndicator.gameObject.activeSelf != step.Charging`.
findings.vnote: PointingBeamController.cs:279 makes two Camera.main calls per frame, only for the player, only in ASSIST with HasAim, and only when a reticle is assigned (bots have none). UpdateChargeIndicator (line 240) calls SetActive every frame for the player only; chargeIndicator is null on bots. No allocation; trivial cost.

findings.title: PrototypeTarget clones its material via renderer.material (practice cubes stay in the arena during RUN)
findings.frequency: once per target at scene load (4 Target_N cubes, HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:143-147). Later color writes are per-hit (OnHit) and per flash end.
findings.detail: Each target cube clones targetMat in Awake (4 instances, created once and never freed, but not a growing leak). The cubes keep their colliders and are not in RunDirector.hideDuringRun (builder line 255 hides only the Quick Match bot), so bot and player beams can hit them during RUN. Each hit then writes to the instanced material. There is no recurring allocation, and Invoke(nameof(Respawn)) runs only per kill.
findings.fix: Use a MaterialPropertyBlock (_BaseColor) for the flash and read the base color from sharedMaterial, as in GC-4.
findings.vnote: PrototypeTarget.cs:20 clones the material once per Target_N cube at load (4 cubes, created in BuildScene for both scenes). The cubes are not in hideDuringRun (builder line 255), so they stay hittable during RUN. Later writes reuse the instance. This is a fixed, one-time cost of 4 materials, not a recurring allocation or a growing leak.

missed.title: Run bots are Instantiate'd and Destroy'ed mid-fight; each spawn builds a ~13-GameObject prefab and allocates (no pooling)
missed.frequency: per-spawn: at island start and again respawnInterval (1.5 s) after each kill while the island still wants bots (Arena islands with BotCount 3 / MaxAlive 2, and every kill on Horde islands). Destroy runs per kill (line 204, corpseTime 0.3 s) and on every island transition (DespawnBots, line 257).
missed.detail: The RunBot prefab (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:684-701) has a root with RunBot, BotInputSource, HandPuppeteerController, PointingBeamController and BotTelegraphLine. It also has RunBotHero (SphereCollider, BeamHitReceiver, AudioSource, FlyingCharacter, HeroHealth, AimAssistTarget), a Visual with 4 mesh renderers, a HealthBar, a GroundMarker (cylinder disc, LineRenderer, HeroGroundMarker) and two more LineRenderers. Each spawn instantiates all of these and runs about 11 Awake/OnEnable calls. Awake does several allocations: HeroHealth.Awake allocates two GetComponentsInChildren arrays and clones 4 materials (GC-4). BotInputSource.Awake allocates a BotBrain and a new System.Random (an int[56] table; BotInputSource.cs:45 to BotBrain.cs:109). Setup then calls SetHealthScale, ResetHealth and Respawn, which allocates another Renderer[] (GC-5). RunDirector adds a closure and delegate per spawn. Each kill Destroys the whole hierarchy 0.3 s later. Spawns happen during combat, which makes this the largest per-event cost in this dimension. It is probably a hitch of a few milliseconds per spawn on Quest, not a multi-second freeze, but that is unmeasured. The user explicitly asked for bot pooling.
missed.fix: Pool RunBot instances in RunDirector. Pre-warm MaxAlive (2) plus 1 inactive bots under the arena at Awake. SpawnBot activates one, calls Setup (which already resets health, scale and enemy) and resets BotBrain through OnEnable. OnBotDied and DespawnBots deactivate the bot after corpseTime with a timer instead of calling Destroy. Subscribe Died once per pooled bot with a cached handler instead of a new closure per spawn. Together with an MPB tint in HeroHealth (GC-4), this removes per-spawn material clones and the leak.

missed.title: RunChoiceMenu.ShopKey boxes the IReadOnlyList enumerator every frame during the Shop phase
missed.code: foreach (ShopSlot slot in shop.Slots) key = key * 2 + (slot.Sold ? 1 : 0);
missed.frequency: per-frame (LateUpdate, line 107-111) while the run is in RunPhase.Shop and the choice menu is showing.
missed.detail: Shop.Slots is declared as IReadOnlyList<ShopSlot> (Economy.cs:121), so this foreach boxes List<ShopSlot>.Enumerator each frame. This is the same mechanism as GC-1. It runs only on the shop screen, not during island combat, so it cannot explain an in-fight freeze. It is listed so the GC-1 fix pass covers both instances of the pattern.
missed.fix: Index loop: `var slots = shop.Slots; for (int i = 0; i < slots.Count; i++) key = key * 2 + (slots[i].Sold ? 1 : 0);`

dimensions.notes:
Scope checked: every file in HandProto/Match (all 12 are referenced by Arena_Main.unity; RunBot is in the RunBot.prefab), plus the Core code they call every frame (RunStateMachine, MatchStateMachine, RunHudText, RunChoiceText, TutorialSequencer, BotBrain). For context I also read HeroStats, Inventory, Economy, ItemDefinition, RunHeroStats, BotInputSource and HeroHealth lines 60-99.

Clean (no per-frame heap allocation found): MatchStateMachine.Tick, RunStateMachine.Tick, TutorialSequencer.Tick, BotBrain.Step (all structs; HandInputData and ArenaBounds are structs), HandMenu.LateUpdate, WristMenu.Update, TutorialDirector.Update, AimModeSetting, ArenaViewMode (event-only), RunBot. WristMenu line 69 and TutorialDirector line 155 assign the same literal or serialized string instance each frame, and TMP returns early on equal strings, so no mesh rebuild. RunDirector.UpdateSpawning `_bots.RemoveAll(b => b == null)` (line 172) uses a non-capturing lambda, which Roslyn caches, so it does not allocate. RunDirector.ApplyControls (lines 162-168) uses foreach over List<T>, a struct enumerator. There is no Debug.Log, LINQ, Find*/FindObjectOfType or renderer.material in any in-scope file (grep-verified).

Verified engine facts used above:
(1) TMP (com.unity.ugui 2.6.0) TMP_Text.text setter returns early when the new string equals the current one (TMP_Text.cs:128), so per-frame .text costs only the allocation plus the compare.
(2) TMP SetText(string, float...) always marks the text dirty and rebuilds the mesh, with no equality check (TMP_Text.cs:2915-2928). Calling SetText every frame would make CPU worse; dirty-check first.
(3) I disassembled Unity's unityaot-linux mscorlib (read-only, into the scratchpad). String.Format with 1-3 args uses a ParamsArray struct, and AppendFormatHelper uses ISpanFormattable, so each interpolation hole costs one boxed int. 4+ holes add an object[]. I assumed this AOT profile matches the Android IL2CPP BCL.
(4) UnityEngine.XRModule InputDevices.GetDevicesWithCharacteristics is allocation-free (static s_InputDeviceList).

Trivial per-frame native calls, not reported as findings: unguarded SetActive in MatchHud.cs:36 and :44 and in TutorialDirector.cs:153, 154, 211 (these early-out natively on an equal state); RunDirector.ApplyControls reads input.enabled per bot per frame; HandMenu sets pointer.enabled every frame.

Out of dimension, but it makes GM-6 worse: HeroHealth.cs:81 clones a material per renderer in Awake (per bot spawn, leaked after Destroy), and HeroHealth.cs:245/252 and HandPuppeteerController.cs:82/90 use .material. Inventory.Add (Inventory.cs:59) allocates a FindIndex closure per pick.

Both directors serialize debugKeys: 1 in Arena_Main (lines 8530/8560). This is harmless on the Quest unless a keyboard is paired.

Order for the fix pass: GM-6 (pooling + one spawn per frame) and GM-1/GM-2/GM-3 (dirty-checked HUD) first; these are the only items here that allocate during island combat. In the PerfSpikeLogger, logging RunPhase, BotsAlive and whether a spawn happened that frame would directly separate the spawn-spike hypothesis from the GC hypothesis.

findings.title: RUN status line is rebuilt from scratch and assigned to TMP every frame (RunHudText.Status/Objective)
findings.code:
else if (inRun) scoreLine.text = RunStatusText(r);
...
string head = $"ISLAND {island}/{RunRules.IslandCount}  {IslandName(type)}";  // RunHudText.cs:25
return head + $"\n<size=80%>HP {hp}/{Mathf.RoundToInt(maxHealth)}    {crystals} CRYSTALS</size>";  // RunHudText.cs:28
findings.frequency: per-frame (MatchHud.LateUpdate) in every RUN phase except Victory/Defeat: Intro, Island, IslandCleared, OpenChest, Shop, ChoosePortal, and also while paused
findings.detail: MatchHud.LateUpdate (lines 31-39) calls RunStatusText (56-66) every frame, which calls RunHudText.Objective (RunHudText.cs:12-20) and RunHudText.Status (22-29). Per frame on an Arena/Elite island that is: Objective `$"{botsLeft} BOTS LEFT"` (1 boxed int + 1 string), IslandName (enum ToString + ToUpperInvariant = at least 1 new string), the head format (2 boxed ints + 1 string), `head += "  -  " + objective` (1 concat string), the HP/crystals format (3 boxed ints + 1 string) and the final `head + ...` concat (1 string). On Horde, Objective also calls Clock (RunHudText.cs:49: 2 boxes + 1 string) and a `"SURVIVE " +` concat. I checked the Unity AOT mscorlib IL: String.Format with 1-3 args uses a ParamsArray struct and AppendFormatHelper formats ints through ISpanFormattable, so each hole costs one boxed int (~24 B) and no temp strings. My rough estimate is 0.7-0.9 KB of garbage per frame, about 50-80 KB/s at 72-90 Hz and about 30-45 MB over a 10-minute run, from this one line of text. The string content changes only when HP, crystals, kills or the Horde second changes. TMP's text setter returns early on an equal string (TMP_Text.cs:128), so the mesh is not rebuilt every frame and the cost is purely the allocations plus an O(n) compare. This is the only continuous per-frame allocator in this dimension during island combat, so it feeds the GC cycles that are the top freeze suspect. How much it contributes to a freeze still needs to be measured on the device.
findings.fix: In MatchHud, cache the ints that drive the line: island, (int)spec.Type, botsLeft, horde seconds = Mathf.CeilToInt(hordeLeft), crystals, Mathf.RoundToInt(hp), Mathf.RoundToInt(maxHp) and whether the objective shows. Rebuild the string and assign scoreLine.text only when one of them differs from the cached value. Reset the cache when the phase changes or the text goes inactive. Optionally cache the 'ISLAND n/9  NAME' head per island, since it changes once per island. Do NOT replace this with a per-frame TMP SetText(format, floats...) call: SetText always sets m_havePropertiesChanged and rebuilds the mesh with no equality check (TMP_Text.cs:2915-2928), which is worse than the current .text assignment. Dirty-check first, then assign.
findings.vnote: The code is at MatchHud.cs:38 and RunHudText.cs:25-28. LateUpdate runs it every frame whenever r != null and the phase is not Victory/Defeat. That includes paused frames: `inRun` ignores IsPaused, and LateUpdate still runs at timeScale 0. MatchHud is in Arena_Main.unity, the only enabled build scene. The project builds with LangVersion 9.0 (Assembly-CSharp.csproj:18), so `$"..."` lowers to string.Format with boxed ints, not an interpolation handler. TMP_Text.cs:128 does return early on an equal string, so the mesh is not rebuilt every frame. My allocation estimate (~0.6-0.8 KB/frame, ~50 KB/s at 72 Hz) matches the finder's. I lowered the impact from high: gcIncremental is 1, so collections are time-sliced. At this rate a GC cycle happens every few minutes, which fits the 'random' timing, but this allocator alone is unlikely to cause a multi-frame freeze. It is still the only continuous per-frame allocator in the match code during combat, and the dirty-check fix is cheap and correct.

findings.title: IslandName allocates through enum ToString + ToUpperInvariant on every call (called every frame)
findings.code: public static string IslandName(IslandType type) => type.ToString().ToUpperInvariant();
findings.frequency: per-frame: once per frame from Status (line 25) in every RUN phase except Victory/Defeat, and twice per frame during Intro (also IntroBanner line 33)
findings.detail: Enum.ToString() on the Mono/IL2CPP BCL boxes the value and looks up the name through the enum metadata cache. ToUpperInvariant (String::ToUpperInvariant -> TextInfo::ToUpper in the AOT mscorlib) returns a new string, and a PascalCase name like 'Arena' always changes, so it can never return the original instance. That is at least 1-2 allocations and a reflection-backed lookup per call, for a value with only 4 possible results. The same pattern is in RunChoiceText.cs:15 (ChestName), 19 (PortalLabel) and 85 (Rarity), but those run only per panel refresh.

Do the same for ChestName and Rarity in RunChoiceText. With GM-1's dirty-check in place, the remaining calls happen only when the text changes.
findings.vnote: RunHudText.cs:9 is called every frame from Status, and twice per frame during Intro (IntroBanner line 33). The IL2CPP Mono BCL boxes the enum and takes the cached name, and ToUpperInvariant always makes a new string for 'Arena' and the other names. Small correction: IslandType has 5 values (Arena, Horde, Elite, Shop, Boss; PortalRoller.cs:8), not 4. This is part of the GM-1 garbage and goes away with GM-1's dirty-check, so on its own the impact is low.

findings.title: Island intro banner string rebuilt every frame although it changes once per second

findings.vnote: MatchHud.cs:74 calls IntroBanner (RunHudText.cs:33-34) every frame in RunPhase.Intro, about 3 s per island. The `+ Mathf.CeilToInt(...)` concat boxes an int. Correction: no bots spawn during Intro. UpdateSpawning runs only in RunPhase.Island (RunDirector.cs:117), so these frames do not overlap the spawn spike. findings.title: Run bots are Instantiate'd / Destroy'ed per spawn and per kill, several in one frame, and each spawn clones materials that are never freed
findings.code:
RunBot bot = Instantiate(botPrefab, at, Quaternion.identity, arena);
...
if (bot.Health != null) bot.Health.Died += () => OnBotDied(bot);   // line 195
if (bot != null) Destroy(bot.gameObject, corpseTime);              // line 204
findings.frequency: per-spawn / per-kill: every island start (2 bots in one frame on Arena islands 3+ and Horde, via the while loop at line 178), every Horde respawn (1.5 s after each kill, for 45 s), and DespawnBots (line 257) on every Intro/IslandCleared/Victory/Defeat
findings.detail: RunBot.prefab has 12 GameObjects, 10 MonoBehaviours, 3 LineRenderers, 6 MeshRenderers, an AudioSource and a SphereCollider. Each Instantiate runs every Awake/OnEnable. HeroHealth.Awake (HeroHealth.cs:74-81, read for context) calls GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>() and GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>() (two new arrays) and `_baseColors.Add(r.material.color)`, which clones a Material for every renderer, LineRenderers included. Destroy(gameObject) does not destroy materials created through renderer.material, so roughly 7-9 Material instances are leaked per bot and pile up across the run until scene unload or UnloadUnusedAssets. BotInputSource.Awake (BotInputSource.cs:45) also allocates a BotBrain and a System.Random per spawn. The `while (_run.WantsSpawn(...) && SpawnBot())` loop creates every missing bot in the same frame, so the cost of 2 spawns lands in one frame at island start, together with the 'FIGHT!' banner text rebuild. Spawn and kill timing depends on combat, not on a particular island, which fits the 'random freeze' report. The spike size is not measured; a PerfSpikeLogger entry tagged with the RunPhase would confirm or rule this out.
findings.fix: Pool RunBots in RunDirector. Pre-instantiate MaxAlive+1 (3) at run start or in Awake, all inactive. On spawn, take one from the pool, set its position, call Setup(), reset HeroHealth (ResetHealth), BotBrain (Reset) and beam/telegraph state, then SetActive(true). On death, start a corpse timer (corpseTime) and return the bot to the pool with SetActive(false) instead of Destroy. In DespawnBots, return every bot to the pool. Subscribe Died once per pooled instance (e.g. RunBot raises its own event with itself as the argument): the current per-spawn lambda at line 195 would stack duplicate handlers if an instance were reused. Spawn at most one bot per frame (replace the while loop with an if). Separately, HeroHealth should tint through MaterialPropertyBlock/sharedMaterial so pooled or not, no Material clones are created (owned by the renderer.material dimension).
findings.vnote: Code verified at RunDirector.cs:192/195/204/257. The `while` at line 178 creates 2 bots in one frame on Arena islands 3+ (BotCount 2-3, MaxAlive 2) and on Horde, and Horde respawns 1.5 s after each kill. The prefab counts are right: 12 GOs, 10 MBs, 3 LineRenderers, 6 MeshRenderers, 1 AudioSource, 1 SphereCollider. Correction on the Material leak: HeroHealth sits on the child RunBotHero, not on the root, and line 79 skips HealthBar through IsChildOf(healthBarFill). The 3 LineRenderers (BotBeamRenderer, BotTelegraphRenderer, GroundMarker) and Disc are siblings under the RunBot root. So each bot clones exactly 4 Materials (Body, Nose, Fin_L, Fin_R), not 7-9, and no LineRenderer materials. These clones are never destroyed, as Unity's renderer.material docs say. The scene never reloads, so they pile up across runs. BotInputSource is disabled in the prefab (m_Enabled: 0), but its Awake still runs on Instantiate, so a BotBrain and a System.Random are allocated per spawn. The spike is real but not measured; it is more likely a dropped frame or two than a multi-second freeze, hence medium.

findings.title: ShopKey foreach over IReadOnlyList boxes an enumerator every frame in the shop

findings.frequency: per-frame (RunChoiceMenu.LateUpdate line 109) while RunPhase.Shop is showing

The key exists only to catch debug-key purchases.

findings.vnote: RunChoiceMenu.cs:193. Shop.Slots is IReadOnlyList<ShopSlot> backed by a List (Economy.cs:111,121), so foreach boxes List<T>.Enumerator. It runs every frame in RunPhase.Shop only (lines 107-112). About 40 B/frame, out of combat.

findings.title: Choice-panel refresh allocates closures, a layout array and label strings per refresh
findings.frequency: per-event: panel phase change, purchase, reroll, debug-key change (_dirty); also `Choose(run.RerollShop)` / `Choose(run.LeaveShop)` (lines 82-83) build a new Func<bool> per press

RunChoiceText.Layout (RunChoiceText.cs:73) allocates a new Vector2[] per refresh. ItemCard, ShopSlot, PortalLabel, ChestHeader and RerollLabel each build 1-3 strings plus enum ToString/ToUpperInvariant (RunChoiceText.cs:15, 19, 85). All out of combat, not a freeze source.

findings.title: RunStateMachine.Stats refolds the whole inventory (boxed enumerators) on every access
findings.code: public HeroStats Stats => HeroStats.From(Inventory);
findings.frequency: per-event: every bot kill (line 201 KillReward(Stats)), every clear (line 328 ClearReward and line 232 HealAfterClear), every player death (line 169 RevivesLeft via line 218); also ChestRoller.cs:40 per chest
findings.detail: HeroStats.From (HeroStats.cs:80-84) iterates `inventory.Items` (IReadOnlyList<OwnedItem>) and each item's `Effects` and `Debuffs` (IReadOnlyList<StatEffect>) with foreach. Every one of those boxes an enumerator: 1 + up to 2 per owned item, plus the fold work. RunHeroStats already caches the same fold by Inventory.TotalLevels (RunHeroStats.cs:18-30), but the state machine does not. This allocation happens once per kill or clear, so it is small, but kills happen in combat frames.
findings.fix: Cache in RunStateMachine: keep a `_statsLevels` int and a `_stats` HeroStats, and recompute only when Inventory.TotalLevels changes or Inventory is replaced in StartRun. In HeroStats.From, use indexed for loops over Items, Effects and Debuffs so it never boxes.
findings.vnote: RunStateMachine.cs:149 refolds the inventory on every access. It is reached from ReportBotKilled (line 201), ClearIsland (328), HealAfterClear (232) and RevivesLeft (169). HeroStats.From foreaches over IReadOnlyList<OwnedItem> (a List) and IReadOnlyList<StatEffect> (StatEffect[] arrays, ItemDefinition.cs:71-72,89-90), so it boxes or allocates an enumerator per non-empty collection. That is a few hundred bytes per kill at most. Negligible.

findings.title: Bots spawned in the same frame can share an identical RNG seed (TickCount): lock-step strafing and firing
findings.code: _brain = new BotBrain(CurrentParams(), seed != 0 ? seed : System.Environment.TickCount);
findings.frequency: per-spawn (BotBrain.cs:109 `_rng = new System.Random(seed);`)
findings.detail: This is a correctness bug, not a performance one. RunBot.prefab serializes `seed: 0` (RunBot.prefab:898), so every run bot seeds from Environment.TickCount, which has millisecond resolution. RunDirector.UpdateSpawning spawns all missing bots in one frame (RunDirector.cs:178). When both Awake calls land in the same millisecond, the two BotBrains get identical System.Random streams. Their initial strafe timer (Reset -> NextStrafeSwitch), fire jitter (lines 276/287), aim error (318-325) and evade side (302-303) then match. Their positions differ, but their shot timing and dodge choices stay in lock step. Whether the seeds collide depends on how long one Instantiate takes on the device, so this does not reproduce every time. Each spawn also allocates a System.Random (int[56]); pooling (GM-6) removes that.
findings.fix: Have RunDirector hand each bot a distinct seed from its own seeded _rng: add a seed parameter to RunBot.Setup that forwards to a new BotInputSource.Reseed(int), which rebuilds the brain's RNG or adds a BotBrain.Reseed. Alternatively mix in a per-spawn counter or GetInstanceID() when seed == 0.
findings.vnote: Verified: the prefab has `seed: 0` on BotInputSource (RunBot.prefab:898), BotInputSource.cs:45 seeds from TickCount, and Awake runs on Instantiate. Two bots from the same `while` loop share a seed only if both Awakes land in the same millisecond, which depends on how long Instantiate takes on the device. Their paths also split once either bot is hit, because StartEvade draws from the RNG. Important gap in the proposed fix: BotBrain.Reset sets `_fireTimer = _p.FireInterval` with no jitter (BotBrain.cs:136). Both bots are enabled in the same frame (SetControlled at RunDirector.cs:194 -> OnEnable -> Reset), so their first telegraph and shot are in sync even with distinct seeds. See the missed item.

findings.title: Headset presence check enumerates all XR devices through native calls every frame
findings.frequency: per-frame (MatchDirector.Update, pauseOnHeadsetRemoved = true), in every phase
findings.detail: I verified the UnityEngine.XRModule IL: GetDevicesWithCharacteristics refills a static s_InputDeviceList through native GetDevices_Internal and calls the native get_characteristics on every device. It makes no managed allocation, so this is not a GC source. It is still several managed-to-native transitions per frame (all head, hand and eye devices), plus a string-keyed native TryGetFeatureValue, just to detect the headset being taken off.
findings.fix: Cache the head InputDevice: look it up once, then again only when `!_head.isValid` or on InputDevices.deviceConnected/deviceDisconnected. Optionally poll userPresence every ~0.2 s on unscaled time instead of every frame.
findings.vnote: MatchDirector.cs:206-208 runs every frame from Update. pauseOnHeadsetRemoved is 1 in Arena_Main.unity:8559. The list is a reused field, and I agree it makes no managed allocation. The native calls per frame are minor overhead only. Not a freeze source.

findings.title: Menu pointer raycasts against every layer and calls GetComponent per hit every frame while a menu is up
findings.frequency: per-frame while HandMenu enables the pointer: main menu, pause, end panels and RUN choice panels (OpenChest/Shop/ChoosePortal)
findings.detail: There is no managed allocation: RaycastNonAlloc uses a static buffer, and I believe GetComponent's not-found allocation only happens in the Editor, not in player builds (not verified). But the ~0 mask with Collide hits the arena walls, heroes, bots and their trigger colliders, and each hit costs a native .collider plus a GetComponent call. There is also a correctness edge: the RaycastNonAlloc buffer is unsorted and capped at 32, so in a busy scene the nearest button can be dropped.
findings.fix: Put the HandMenuButton colliders on a dedicated menu layer (set by HandHeroSceneBuilder) and pass that LayerMask. Use TryGetComponent. With a menu-only mask, the 32-hit cap no longer matters.
findings.vnote: HandMenuPointer.cs:93/99 runs every frame while HandMenu enables the pointer (HandMenu.cs:41: main, paused, end, run choice). RaycastNonAlloc uses a static buffer. GetComponent returning null does not allocate in player builds; the fake-null allocation is Editor-only. The mask is ~0 and triggers are included, but bots are already despawned during the choice phases, so very few colliders get hit and the 32-hit cap is theoretical. A menu layer mask is a fine cleanup but not a perf issue.

_block.SetColor("_Color", c);

missed.title: Simultaneously spawned bots always fire their first shot in the same frame (fire timer not jittered on Reset)
missed.frequency: per-spawn (every island start with 2 bots, Horde double respawns)
missed.detail: RunDirector.SpawnBot calls SetControlled(true) right after Instantiate (RunDirector.cs:194). That fires BotInputSource.OnEnable -> _brain.Reset() for both bots in the same frame. Reset sets _fireTimer to the fixed FireInterval with no random jitter, and UpdateShooting counts it down by the same dt for both. As long as both perceive the player within MaxFireRange (40 m, and the arena is 35 m wide), both bots start telegraphing and fire in the same frame, whatever their RNG seeds are. The player sees two red lines appear at once on every Arena 3+ and Horde start, which may be harder to read than intended. GM-10's per-bot seed fix does not change this.
missed.fix: In BotBrain.Reset, add jitter to the first shot: `_fireTimer = _p.FireInterval + (float)_rng.NextDouble() * _p.FireIntervalJitter;`, or let RunDirector stagger spawns, for example one bot per frame with a short delay between them. Combine with GM-10's distinct seeds so the jitter itself differs per bot. Pure logic, so add an EditMode test that two brains with different seeds get different first fire times.

missed.title: HeroHealth.SetVisible allocates a Renderer[] on every bot spawn and every kill
missed.code: foreach (Renderer r in GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true)) r.enabled = visible;
missed.frequency: per-spawn (Setup -> SetHealthScale -> ResetHealth -> Respawn -> SetVisible(true)) and per-kill (Die -> SetVisible(false)); also per player death/revive
missed.detail: GetComponentsInChildren returns a new array on each call and walks the whole RunBotHero subtree, including inactive objects. For a bot that is 5 renderers (Body, Nose, Fin_L, Fin_R, HealthBar). It is a small allocation, but it lands in the same frames as the Instantiate/Destroy spikes from GM-6. Pooling bots does not remove it, because a reused bot still goes through ResetHealth -> Respawn -> SetVisible(true).
missed.fix: Cache every renderer once in Awake, including the health bar, in a separate List<Renderer> (or use the non-allocating GetComponentsInChildren(true, list) overload into a reused list), and loop over that cached list in SetVisible. Do this together with the bot pooling and the MaterialPropertyBlock tint changes.

dimensions.notes:
Runtime spawn sites in game code: there are only two. One is RunDirector.SpawnBot (RunDirector.cs:192) with its Destroys at RunDirector.cs:204 and :257. The other is PointingBeamController.Fire (PointingBeamController.cs:372-373). A grep of Scripts/HandProto and Scripts/Core found no runtime new GameObject, AddComponent, new Material, new Mesh or CreatePrimitive. Those all live in Editor/HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs. Several objects named in the task already reuse pre-built objects and need no pooling. The player BeamRenderer and the bots' BotBeamRenderer are one LineRenderer each, toggled through .enabled. BotTelegraphLine, the ShockwaveController ring, LockOnRing, HeroGroundMarker (disc + drop line) and the HealthBar cube are also reused. The run choice panels and cards (3 portal buttons, 4 chest cards, 4 shop slots, REROLL, LEAVE) are built once by HandHeroSceneBuilder.RunChoicePanels and shown with SetActive. RunChoiceMenu.ShowButtons allocates a small Vector2[] and closures per refresh. That happens per event and is negligible.

Pooling targets ranked by expected spike size:
1. RunBot (SP-1/SP-4). Biggest per event; 2 instantiates in the same frame at every 'FIGHT!' on 2-bot islands, plus Horde churn. Pool size MaxAlive + 1 = 3.
2. BeamImpact (SP-3). Smallest per event, most frequent (per hitting shot). Ring pool of ~8.
Nothing else needs pooling.

Leaks across islands and runs: only SP-2 (4 material clones per spawned bot) grows without bound for the whole session, because the scene is never reloaded. Other state is clean:
- Event subscriptions are balanced: HeroHealth Hit, BotInputSource Hit, PointingBeamController Respawned, MatchDirector/RunDirector Died and TutorialDirector Hit all have matching OnEnable/OnDisable pairs.
- Awake-only subscriptions are on objects owned by the same component (_match, _run), so they cannot leak.
- TutorialDirector.Begin creates a new TutorialSequencer per tutorial. The old one is unreferenced and gets collected.
- AimAssistTarget.Registry removes entries in OnDisable. RunDirector._bots is cleared. Inventory, CrystalWallet and Shop are recreated per run.
- Benign dangling reference: when a bot is destroyed while the player's aim hand is untracked, PointingBeamController._assistTarget and LockOnRing._target keep pointing at the destroyed object. Both are checked with Unity's overloaded == / null, so nothing crashes, and they clear on the next aimed frame.

Realistic assessment: spawn churn causes one-frame hitches that line up with island starts and kills, plus a small steady stream of garbage. On its own it is unlikely to explain a multi-hundred-ms random freeze. The PerfSpikeLogger should record RunDirector.BotsAlive and the RunPhase, so spikes can be matched to spawn and kill frames.

Pooled-bot reset checklist, for whoever implements SP-1:
- Spawn position (HeroHealth._spawnPosition).
- Single Died subscription.
- Beam enabled state and _beamTimer, plus _rawAimPoint / ShotCooldown in PointingBeamController.
- These already reset themselves: BotBrain (OnEnable -> Reset), FlyingCharacter (Respawn), HeroHealth model and colors (ResetHealth), AimAssistTarget (OnEnable), BotTelegraphLine (hides while input is disabled).
- Seed per bot (SP-7).

Cross-dimension items seen while reading, left for the GC/TMP auditors and not counted as SP findings:
- MatchHud.LateUpdate sets scoreLine.text and banner.text every frame (MatchHud.cs:37-38, 45). That builds a new string and rebuilds the TMP mesh each frame during a run.
- PointingBeamController.CollectCandidates loops `foreach` over IReadOnlyList AimAssistTarget.All (line 324). That boxes an enumerator per frame for every controller with aim, which includes every live run bot, so it scales with spawns.
- HandGestureTracker.FindSubsystem allocates `new List<XRHandSubsystem>()` (line 110) and builds strings (lines 133-136) every frame while no hand subsystem is running.
- DynamicsManager m_AutoSyncTransforms: 1.

Legacy check: Arena_Main.unity is the only enabled build scene, and it references none of the root Scripts/*.cs GUIDs. The LoadScene and DontDestroyOnLoad calls in GameManager, VictoryPanel, GameOverPanel, MenuManager, RestartGame and AudioManager are not in the build. Spike sizes are estimates from reading the code; nothing was profiled.

findings.title: RunBot prefab is Instantiated for every bot spawn (12 GameObjects, 27 components, 4 material clones), up to 2 in the same frame when the fight starts
findings.code:
while (_run.WantsSpawn(_bots.Count) && SpawnBot()) { }   // line 178
RunBot bot = Instantiate(botPrefab, at, Quaternion.identity, arena);   // line 192
findings.frequency: per bot spawn. On the first Island frame 1-2 spawns land in the same frame, because Spec.MaxAlive = 2 on Arena islands 3-8 and on Horde. After that it is 1 spawn per kill, 1.5 s after the kill (respawnInterval), on Horde (45 s) and on multi-bot Arena islands. Estimate: about 15-40 spawns per run.
findings.detail: RunBot.prefab contents. Root RunBot holds BotInputSource (disabled), HandPuppeteerController, PointingBeamController, BotTelegraphLine and RunBot. Its children are: BotBeamRenderer (LineRenderer), BotTelegraphRenderer (LineRenderer), RunBotHero_GroundMarker (LineRenderer + HeroGroundMarker, with a Disc cylinder MeshRenderer child) and RunBotHero. RunBotHero has a SphereCollider (r 0.9), BeamHitReceiver, AudioSource, FlyingCharacter, HeroHealth and AimAssistTarget, plus Body/Nose/Fin_L/Fin_R Lit MeshRenderers under Visual and a HealthBar Unlit cube. The AudioSource never plays because fireSound is null in the prefab. That makes 12 GameObjects and 27 non-Transform components, with no TMP, no lights and no Rigidbody. One spawn does all of the following on the main thread in one frame: Instantiate; every Awake; HeroHealth.Awake with GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>, GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer> and r.material on 4 renderers (4 Material clones, see SP-2); BotInputSource.Awake with new BotBrain + new System.Random; Setup -> SetHealthScale -> ResetHealth -> Respawn -> another GetComponentsInChildren (SP-5); SetControlled(true) -> OnEnable -> delegate subscription; the closure at line 195; and inserting a static collider into the physics scene. This is the largest spawn event in the game. It lands on the first 'FIGHT!' frame of every island (doubled there) and mid-fight on Horde. The cost on Quest 3 has not been measured. Expect a one-frame hitch plus managed garbage, not a multi-second freeze.
findings.fix: Pool the bots in RunDirector. Prewarm rules.MaxAlive + 1 (3) inactive RunBots under `arena` in Awake (scene load, not mid-run). SpawnBot takes an inactive bot, calls SetPositionAndRotation(at, identity), SetActive(true), Setup (with the new spawn position, see SP-6), then SetControlled. OnBotDied queues the bot for return after corpseTime using a float timer checked in Update (no coroutine/WaitForSeconds allocation) and then calls SetActive(false). DespawnBots calls SetActive(false) instead of Destroy. Subscribe Died once per pooled bot at prewarm. The prefab and the builder stay as they are.
findings.vnote: Code verified at RunDirector.cs:178 (while loop) and :192 (Instantiate with parent arena). Frequency verified: RunRules.Island (RunStateMachine.cs:92-97) gives MaxAlive = min(BotCount, 2) = 2 on Arena islands 3-8 and 2 on Horde, so the first Island frame spawns 2 bots back to back. After that, OnBotDied sets _spawnTimer = respawnInterval (1.5 s). Prefab contents verified in RunBot.prefab: 12 GameObjects; 27 non-Transform components (5 on the root, 6 on RunBotHero, 5x MeshFilter+MeshRenderer, Disc MF+MR, GroundMarker LR+HeroGroundMarker, 2 LineRenderers); no Rigidbody; fireSound {fileID: 0}. BotInputSource is disabled in the prefab (m_Enabled: 0), but Unity still runs its Awake because the GameObject is active, so new BotBrain + System.Random do happen. botPrefab is a serialized scene reference, so the spawn does no disk IO. The mechanism is real (Instantiate, all Awakes, 4 material clones, 2 GetComponentsInChildren arrays, delegate and closure allocations, static collider insert). I lowered the impact from high to medium: this is one small prefab per event, probably a few ms on Quest 3 (not measured), and it fires at predictable moments (fight start, Horde respawns), while the developer describes freezes as random. It can drop a frame but is unlikely to explain a visible freeze by itself. Pooling is still the right fix, but see missed item SP-9: naive pooling adds a movement bug.

findings.title: HeroHealth.Awake clones 4 materials per spawned bot via renderer.material and never destroys them: native leak across islands and runs
findings.frequency: per bot spawn (Awake): 4 clones each (Body, Nose, Fin_L, Fin_R; HealthBar is excluded). With 15-40 bots per run that is about 60-160 leaked Materials per run. SetColor (line 245) and RestoreColors (line 252) then write r.material.color on every hit, stun and respawn. Those calls reuse the clone and do not allocate again.
findings.detail: Renderer.material clones the shared material on first access. Unity documents that the caller must Destroy the clone, and only Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets (normally run on scene load) reclaims it otherwise. The game never reloads Arena_Main, the only enabled build scene: game code has no LoadScene or UnloadUnusedAssets call, and the legacy LoadScene scripts are not referenced by the scene. So every destroyed run bot leaves 4 URP Lit material clones (of Hero_Bot.mat / Hero_Nose.mat) in native memory for the rest of the app session, and the count grows with every island and every run. Each clone is also a separate SRP Batcher material that is set up during the spawn frame. This is the only unbounded cross-island/cross-run growth found in the SPAWN dimension. The player hero, the Quick Match bot and the 4 PrototypeTargets clone once each, which is bounded and fine.
findings.fix: Store the clones once: in Awake use `Material m = r.material; _materials.Add(m); _baseColors.Add(m.color);`. Write `_materials[i].color` in SetColor and RestoreColors, and add `OnDestroy(){ foreach (Material m in _materials) if (m != null) Destroy(m); }`. Bot pooling (SP-1) also caps the count at the pool size. Alternative: MaterialPropertyBlock with _BaseColor/_Color, as HandMenuButton does. That avoids clones entirely, but those renderers then leave the SRP Batcher path.
findings.vnote: HeroHealth.cs:77-82 verified: r.material on every Renderer under RunBotHero except the HealthBar. healthBarFill is the HealthBar transform itself (prefab line 549), and IsChildOf(self) is true, so it is skipped. That leaves 4 clones per bot: Body, Fin_L and Fin_R from Hero_Bot.mat, Nose from Hero_Nose.mat, both URP Lit. The game code (HandProto + Core) has no Destroy of materials and no LoadScene or UnloadUnusedAssets call (grep). Only Arena_Main is enabled in EditorBuildSettings, and none of the legacy root scripts are referenced by it (GUID check). The leak is real. SetColor/RestoreColors reuse the instance. I rated the impact low: the leaked clones are native objects that no longer render after the bot is destroyed, so they add no per-frame, GC or SRP Batcher cost. The cost is a slow memory growth of about 100+ small materials per run, which only matters in very long sessions. It will not cause hitches. The fix is correct.

findings.title: BeamImpact hit effect is Instantiated and Destroyed on every beam hit (player and all bots)
findings.code:
GameObject fx = Instantiate(hitEffectPrefab, end, Quaternion.LookRotation(-dir));
Destroy(fx, 1f);
findings.frequency: per shot whose ray hits any collider, for every PointingBeamController. All of them reference BeamImpact.prefab: Arena_Main.unity:8283 (player), :16220 (Quick Match bot) and RunBot.prefab:968 (every run bot). In ASSIST mode the player's aim point is itself a raycast hit, so nearly every player shot spawns one: up to ~3/s at the 0.35 s cooldown, more with cooldown-cut items. Each bot adds one per hit, firing about every 2.2-3.2 s.
findings.detail: BeamImpact.prefab is 1 GameObject: Transform, MeshFilter (built-in sphere), MeshRenderer (shared BeamImpact.mat, shadows off) and ImpactFlash. It has no collider and allocates no material (ImpactFlash only scales the transform). ImpactFlash already switches itself off after 0.25 s (ImpactFlash.cs:24) and resets in OnEnable, so each instance sits inactive for 0.75 s and is then destroyed. Every hit therefore costs Instantiate + Destroy + new managed wrappers (GameObject, ImpactFlash). The cost per event is small, but this is the most frequent spawn in the game and it runs continuously in every fight, giving a steady stream of native object churn and GC garbage. The FX is not parented, so destroying a bot does not take its effects with it (no dangling objects).
findings.fix: Add a small shared pool, static or a scene component, keyed by the prefab. Do not parent it under a RunBot, because bots get destroyed or pooled. Prewarm ~8 instances at scene start. Fire takes the next instance from a ring buffer, calls SetPositionAndRotation(end, rot), then SetActive(false) + SetActive(true) to rerun OnEnable. Remove Destroy(fx, 1f). 8 instances at a 0.25 s lifetime cover 32 hits/s. Keep the hitEffectPrefab field as the pool template.
findings.vnote: PointingBeamController.cs:370-374 verified. BeamImpact.prefab is 1 GameObject: Transform, MeshFilter with the built-in sphere (10207), a MeshRenderer with shared BeamImpact.mat (URP Unlit opaque), and ImpactFlash. It has no collider. ImpactFlash.cs:24 self-deactivates at 0.25 s. Three references confirmed: Arena_Main.unity:8283 (player, has aimModeSetting), :16220 (Quick Match bot) and RunBot.prefab:968. Correction: FX only spawn when the Fire raycast hits a collider. The only arena colliders are Floor, BackWall, Pillar_L and Pillar_R (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:129-134), plus hero spheres and targets. Shots toward the open sides or front hit nothing and spawn no FX, so 'nearly every player shot' is overstated. Each spawn is one tiny GameObject with roughly a hundred bytes of managed garbage, at most a few per second across all shooters. Incremental GC is on (gcIncremental: 1). The impact is negligible for freezes, so I lowered it to low. It is a cheap pooling win, and the ring-buffer fix is sound. I also checked for a first-use shader hitch: HealthBar.mat on every hero already uses the same Unlit opaque shader as BeamImpact.mat, so a one-time pipeline compile on the first impact is unlikely.

findings.title: Bots are Destroyed on every kill and on every island transition (12-GameObject hierarchy each)
findings.code:
if (bot != null) Destroy(bot.gameObject, corpseTime);   // line 204, OnBotDied
if (bot != null) Destroy(bot.gameObject);               // line 257, DespawnBots
findings.frequency: per bot kill (delayed 0.3 s), and per island transition for every live bot: Intro (220), IslandCleared (226), Victory/Defeat (239) and EndRun (248). A Horde clear or a Defeat destroys up to 2 bots in the same frame.
findings.detail: Each Destroy tears down 3 LineRenderers and 6 MeshRenderers, removes the static collider from the physics scene, removes the AudioSource, and runs OnDisable on 6 behaviours. HeroHealth, BotInputSource and AimAssistTarget unsubscribe and unregister correctly, so no dangling event handlers are left. The 4 material clones are left behind (SP-2). The IslandCleared frame also runs ClearIsland -> PhaseChanged -> SetHealth and updates the HUD, so the work stacks up in one frame. This is cheaper than Instantiate, but it lands mid-fight on Horde (corpse removal) and on phase-change frames.
findings.fix: Same pool as SP-1: after corpseTime return the bot with SetActive(false) (timer in Update), and have DespawnBots deactivate instead of Destroy.
findings.vnote: RunDirector.cs:204 (Destroy with corpseTime 0.3, scene value at Arena_Main.unity:8528) and :257 verified. DespawnBots is called from Intro (220), IslandCleared (226), Victory/Defeat (239) and EndRun (248). EndRun runs only once, because ReturnToMenu sets the phase to Idle and the next frame exits early. OnDisable paths are balanced: HeroHealth, BotInputSource and AimAssistTarget unsubscribe and unregister. LockOnRing handles a destroyed target through Unity null. Destroy is deferred to the end of the frame, so destroying the shooting bot mid-Fire (bot kills player, then Defeat, then DespawnBots) is safe. The cost is small, so the impact stays low.

findings.title: HeroHealth allocates a new Renderer[] (GetComponentsInChildren) on every death and respawn, and on every bot spawn
findings.code: foreach (Renderer r in GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true)) r.enabled = visible;
findings.frequency: per death (Die -> SetVisible(false)) and per Respawn. Respawn also runs on every ResetHealth: per bot spawn through SetHealthScale, per run start/end, per Quick Match countdown, and per revive. Awake (lines 74 and 77) does two more GetComponentsInChildren per spawn.
findings.detail: GetComponentsInChildren<T>(bool) returns a newly allocated array on each call. The garbage is small (5-6 references), but it lands in the same frames as spawns, kills and phase changes. Awake already walks the same hierarchy, so the array could be cached.
findings.fix: Cache `_allRenderers = GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true)` in Awake (keeping the health bar, unlike _renderers) and loop over it in SetVisible. Or use the List<Renderer> overload with a reused list.
findings.vnote: HeroHealth.cs:239 verified: GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true) returns a new array on every call. It runs from Die (199) and Respawn (209). Respawn is reached from ResetHealth (bot Setup via SetHealthScale, run start/end), Revive and the model respawn tick. Awake has two more calls (74 and 77). Each array holds about 5 references, and these are event-rate calls, not per frame. Impact low.

findings.title: Pooling hazards: per-instance state is captured once (spawn position in Awake, Died closure per spawn, beam state not cleared on disable)
findings.code:
_spawnPosition = transform.position;                        // HeroHealth.cs:73 (Awake only)
if (bot.Health != null) bot.Health.Died += () => OnBotDied(bot);  // RunDirector.cs:195
findings.frequency: per bot spawn. Harmless today because every spawn is a fresh instance; it breaks as soon as SP-1 pooling is added.
findings.detail: Today's state: the closure is allocated per spawn and never unsubscribed. That is not a leak, because the publisher (the bot's HeroHealth) is destroyed with the bot. Each new bot captures its own spawn point in Awake. With naive pooling: (a) subscribing in SpawnBot stacks delegates on the reused HeroHealth, so OnBotDied runs N times per death. The `_bots.Remove` guard at RunDirector.cs:202 hides the extra calls, but the delegate list grows without bound. (b) ResetHealth -> Respawn teleports to the _spawnPosition captured at the first Awake. RunBotHero moves in world space independently of the root, so a reused bot would reappear at a stale spawn point instead of `at`. (c) PointingBeamController.OnDisable (lines 228-235) neither hides the beam nor clears _beamTimer. A bot deactivated mid-beam (beamDuration 0.12 s) can briefly show a stale beam when reused. _rawAimPoint and _shots state also carry over.
findings.fix: When pooling: subscribe Died once per pooled bot at prewarm. Add HeroHealth.SetSpawnPosition(Vector3) and call it from RunBot.Setup(at) before SetHealthScale. In PointingBeamController.OnDisable add `_beamTimer = 0f; if (beam != null) beam.enabled = false; _rawAimPoint = Vector3.zero;`. Optionally reset ShotCooldown pending state there too.
findings.vnote: These are latent hazards that only matter for the pooling fix; they are not bugs today. (a) RunDirector.cs:195 subscribes a new closure per spawn and never unsubscribes. With reuse, the delegates would stack, and the _bots.Remove guard at :202 would hide the duplicate calls. (b) HeroHealth.cs:73 captures _spawnPosition only in Awake, and spawnPoint is {fileID: 0} in the prefab (line 548). Respawn (205-206) would therefore teleport a reused hero to its first spawn point, even though moving the root also moves the RunBotHero child. (c) PointingBeamController.OnDisable (228-235) does not clear _beamTimer or beam.enabled, and _rawAimPoint is smoothed from its old value (line 270). All three verified. The finder missed a more serious hazard of the same kind, the puppeteer clutch (SP-9).

findings.title: Bots spawned in the same frame get Environment.TickCount seeds and an unjittered first fire timer, so they telegraph and fire in lockstep
findings.code: _brain = new BotBrain(CurrentParams(), seed != 0 ? seed : System.Environment.TickCount);
findings.frequency: per bot spawn; matters on the first Island frame of every 2-bot island (Arena 3-8, Horde)
findings.detail: The prefab has seed 0 (RunBot.prefab:898), so each bot seeds from Environment.TickCount, which has millisecond resolution. Two bots instantiated back to back in the while loop at RunDirector.cs:178 can get the same seed. Equal seeds give identical rng streams: fire-interval jitter, strafe-flip timing, aim error and evade side. Separately, both bots are enabled in the same frame (SetControlled -> OnEnable -> BotBrain.Reset sets `_fireTimer = _p.FireInterval` with no jitter, BotBrain.cs:136). So their first telegraph and shot are always simultaneous, and with equal seeds they stay in lockstep until one is hit. The player sees two red lines and takes double damage at the same instant. Confidence is medium because seed equality depends on how long one Instantiate takes. This is a gameplay bug, not a performance one.
findings.fix: Seed bots from RunDirector's own System.Random: add BotInputSource.Reseed(int) and call it from RunBot.Setup with _rng.Next(). Also add random initial jitter in BotBrain.Reset, e.g. `_fireTimer = _p.FireInterval + rng * _p.FireIntervalJitter`. That is a Core logic change, so add or adjust a BotBrain EditMode test.
findings.vnote: Verified BotInputSource.cs:45 (TickCount seed, prefab seed 0 at line 898), BotBrain.Reset sets _fireTimer = _p.FireInterval with no jitter (BotBrain.cs:136), and OnEnable calls Reset (BotInputSource.cs:50). Both bots are enabled in the same SpawnBot loop. MaxFireRange is 40, which is more than the 35 m arena, and both perceive the player on their first Step. So unless the player hits one of them first (StartEvade), their first telegraphs start in the same frame (2.2 s + 0.6 s telegraph). Equal seeds are only plausible, since they depend on whether one Instantiate takes less than 1 ms. 'Lockstep until hit' is overstated: FlipStrafe on a wall pin depends on each bot's position, so the rng consumption diverges. The finder missed two related cases. First, every pause and resume runs SetControlled(false) then SetControlled(true), so OnEnable and Reset run again and all live bots fire in sync once more. Second, Reset uses the Awake-time params, where _fireIntervalScale is still 1, because Params is only refreshed in Sample. The Boss's first shot therefore uses the unscaled 2.2 s instead of 1.54 s. This is a gameplay issue, with low impact.

findings.title: Every spawned bot adds a static SphereCollider (no Rigidbody) that FlyingCharacter moves through the transform every frame, with autoSyncTransforms on
findings.code:
SphereCollider:   # on RunBotHero, m_Radius: 0.9 - no Rigidbody (!u!54) in RunBot.prefab or Arena_Main.unity
transform.position = state.Position;   // FlyingCharacter.cs:125, every frame
findings.frequency: per frame per hero (player, the Quick Match bot when visible, each run bot). The collider is inserted and removed per bot spawn/destroy.
findings.detail: No Rigidbody exists in the prefab or the scene, so every hero collider is a static collider moved by its transform each frame. ProjectSettings/DynamicsManager.asset has m_AutoSyncTransforms: 1, so raycasts issued after those transform writes trigger transform syncs: PointingBeamController.UpdateAim and Fire per controller (player + each bot) per frame, and HandMenuPointer. Unity's guidance is to give colliders that move a kinematic Rigidbody. The cost with 2-4 heroes on Quest 3 has not been measured and is probably small. Check the Physics.SyncColliderTransform / Physics.Processing profiler markers before acting.
findings.fix: In HandHeroSceneBuilder.Hero(), add a kinematic Rigidbody (isKinematic = true, useGravity = false) to the hero root so moving heroes are kinematic actors. Turning autoSyncTransforms off is a behaviour change for raycast timing; measure first.
findings.vnote: RunBot.prefab:382-401 SphereCollider r=0.9 on RunBotHero verified. Zero Rigidbody (!u!54) blocks in RunBot.prefab or Arena_Main.unity. DynamicsManager.asset:22 m_AutoSyncTransforms: 1. FlyingCharacter.cs:125 writes the position every frame. Correction: Fire raycasts once per shot, not per frame; only UpdateAim raycasts every frame for each controller with HasAim. With 2-4 moving static colliders, the transform sync before each raycast is probably negligible on Quest 3. The impact is speculative, so I agree with low confidence and low impact.

missed.title: Pooling hazard: HandPuppeteerController keeps its clutch state across SetActive(false/true), so a bot that was despawned alive and then reused steers to a stale, offset target for its whole life
missed.code:
if (!character.IsAlive) { if (_clutch.IsClutched) OnRelease(); _clutch.Reset(); return; }   // lines 58-63, the only reset
ClutchResult clutch = _clutch.Step(input, character.transform.position, positionScale);   // line 72
missed.frequency: Per reuse of a pooled bot that was returned while alive: Horde clear, Defeat, MENU/EndRun and Intro DespawnBots. This only happens once SP-1/SP-4 pooling is added; with today's Destroy-based code it cannot happen.
missed.detail: ClutchMapper (Core/ClutchMapper.cs) only drops _clutched in Reset(). The puppeteer calls Reset() only while the hero is dead. Today, a bot that dies sits for 0.3 s as a corpse, during which the puppeteer resets, and a pause disables only BotInputSource, so the puppeteer sees ClutchHeld=false and releases. The proposed pool deactivates the whole root, so the puppeteer never sees that release. On reuse: OnEnable calls BotBrain.Reset (_grabbed=false), Setup/Respawn teleports the hero to the new spawn point, and on the first frame the brain sends ClutchHeld=true with zero delta. The puppeteer is still _clutched, so it does not regrab and calls SetTarget(old _target from the previous island). The brain then computes its deltas relative to its own _clutchTarget (the new position), so the mapper target stays offset by (old position - new spawn) for as long as the bot is alive. The visible bug: a reused bot flies to the wrong place, hugs a wall or stays clamped at the arena bounds. Without a reset, this would show up the first time pooling is added.
missed.fix: In HandPuppeteerController add `private void OnDisable() { if (_clutch.IsClutched && character != null) character.ClearTarget(); _clutch.Reset(); }`, or a public ResetClutch() called from RunBot.Setup. Resetting is harmless for the player, who simply regrabs from the hero's position. Add it to the pooling checklist together with the SP-6 items (Died subscribed once, HeroHealth.SetSpawnPosition, clearing the beam timer).

dimensions.notes:
Verdict for RENDER/SETTINGS: nothing in this dimension explains a repeating, random >50 ms freeze. The rendering setup is lean, and runtime code makes no blocking render or IO calls during an island. The likely culprit is still CPU-side work (GC, Instantiate/Destroy of RunBot and BeamImpact, per-frame string building), which other dimensions cover. The highest-value items here are diagnostic: RS-1 frame-timing stats, RS-2 a dev build, RS-6 shader-compile logging and RS-15 pause/focus logging. RS-3 (stack traces) and RS-4 (latency mode) are cheap A/B levers.

Verified as fine, with no finding:
- Player settings: Android scripting backend IL2CPP (ProjectSettings.asset:912 'Android: 1'), ARM64 (:276), Vulkan only with manual APIs (:590 m_APIs 15000000 = 0x15 Vulkan, m_Automatic 0), MT rendering on (:53, :608), graphics jobs off for AndroidPlayer (:580), gcIncremental 1 (:925), static batching on and dynamic off, linear color space.
- Quality: Android default quality is index 1 'Low' (QualitySettings.asset:323), which uses 'Performance URP Config' (HDR off, MSAA 4, render scale 1, no depth or opaque texture, SRP Batcher on, Forward). The renderer is 'Android Preset' with no renderer features, postProcessData null and native render pass on.
- Lighting: one realtime directional light with shadows None (Arena_Main.unity:1702 m_Type: 0). No particle systems, no Rigidbodies, no prefab instances in the scene. Every generated material is opaque (_Surface 0), so the only alpha-blended overdraw is TMP text.
- XR: OpenXR is the only Android loader. Render mode is single-pass instanced/multiview (OpenXRPackageSettings.asset:1523 m_renderMode 1). Enabled Android features are MetaQuest, HandTracking, MetaHandTrackingAim, Meta AR Session/Camera, Meta OpenXRLifeCycle and two controller profiles. SpaceWarp, AutomaticDynamicResolution and DisplayUtilities are off, so the headset runs at the runtime default refresh. Optimize buffer discards is on in MetaQuestFeature. AR Session and ARCameraManager stay disabled outside tabletop mode.
- Hand tracking: the HandGestureTracker/XRHandsInputSource hot path is allocation-free, reads joints only and never starts or stops subsystems (RS-12 covers the not-running path only).
- No runtime Shader.Find, new Material, Resources.Load, File IO, GC.Collect, Thread.Sleep, Application.targetFrameRate or QualitySettings changes in HandProto/Core. LineRenderer recolors use vertex colors. HandMenuButton correctly uses a MaterialPropertyBlock. TMP strings are ASCII, so there is no runtime glyph rasterization from the dynamic fallback font. The Input System uses default dynamic update, so Time.timeScale=0 cannot freeze head pose.

Latent, not active:
- Performance URP Config supports main-light shadows at 4096 with soft shadows, plus additional-light shadows (lines 45-53). This is harmless while the only light casts no shadows, but would be very expensive on Quest if a shadowed light were ever added.
- All six quality levels are kept for Android, so URP stripping keeps variants for the richer pipeline assets as well (build size and load time only).
- Unrelated Resources folders (Vefects 6.5 MB and others) are packed into the APK (build size only).
- m_UseAdaptivePerformance: 1 is a no-op because no Adaptive Performance provider or settings asset exists.

Device context for the report: when a Quest app misses frames, the compositor keeps reprojecting the last frame (the world stops while head rotation still works), and long stalls show the system loading indicator. A 50 ms threshold is about 3.6 frames at 72 Hz.

Honesty notes:
- I modified no repo file. To map TMP components to GameObject names I wrote two throwaway text files, /tmp/tmp_list.txt and /tmp/names.txt, outside the repo, in a read-only grep/awk pipeline. They can be deleted.
- The AUTO/ folder listing changed during my run: BLOCKERS.md, DECISIONS.md, PROGRESS.md, QUESTIONS_FOR_HYUN.md and REPORT_FOR_HYUN.md were listed at first and missing later. I did not touch them; another process (likely the orchestrator) appears to have moved them.
- Build-log facts (shader variant counts, the OpenXR passthrough clear-flag warning at execute.log:652) come from AUTO/logs/execute.log, the last batch build, not a device run.

findings.title: Frame Timing Stats are off, so the planned PerfSpikeLogger cannot tell a CPU stall from a GPU stall
findings.code: enableFrameTimingStats: 0
findings.frequency: once (build setting); affects every frame's measurement
