findings.detail: With Frame Timing Stats disabled, FrameTimingManager.CaptureFrameTimings/GetLatestTimings return no CPU-main, CPU-render or GPU frame times on device. The logger asked for in step 3 can then record only Time.unscaledDeltaTime, and that value cannot separate a main-thread hitch (GC, Instantiate) from a GPU or compositor stall. Nothing in this dimension shows a recurring >50 ms source, so this split is the main lever for root-causing the random freezes.
findings.fix: Set PlayerSettings.enableFrameTimingStats = true (also from BuildScript.ConfigurePlayer). In PerfSpikeLogger, call FrameTimingManager.CaptureFrameTimings() each frame and on a spike log cpuMainThreadFrameTime, cpuRenderThreadFrameTime and gpuFrameTime from a preallocated FrameTiming[1] array, which allocates nothing.
findings.vnote: ProjectSettings.asset:160 really is `enableFrameTimingStats: 0`, and nothing in BuildScript.ConfigurePlayer (lines 82-93) changes it. As far as I know, the release APK's FrameTimingManager returns no CPU or GPU timings with this flag off, so the logger would only get unscaledDeltaTime. One correction: from memory (not stated in the local 6000.6.4f1 XML docs), FrameTimingManager is always on in Development builds, so the dev APK gets the split anyway. Re-rated low: this is diagnostic only and causes no hitch. The preallocated FrameTiming[1] plus GetLatestTimings in the fix does not allocate. There is also a split that needs no build change: on Quest, `adb logcat -s VrApi` prints a line every second with stale frames and GPU% (from memory, not checked on this firmware).

findings.title: BuildScript only produces a non-development APK: no profiler-attachable build, no development-only logging
findings.code: options = BuildOptions.None,
findings.frequency: once per build
findings.detail: Step 4 asks for a Development Build APK, but BuildQuestApk hard-codes BuildOptions.None. Without a development build there is no Unity Profiler or Frame Debugger connection and no on-device profiling, so a freeze cannot be captured as a profiler frame. Any '#if DEVELOPMENT_BUILD' logging also stays compiled out.
findings.fix: Add a second entry point (e.g. BuildQuestApkDev) that uses BuildOptions.Development | BuildOptions.ConnectWithProfiler (optionally AllowDebugging) and writes HandHero_<date>_dev.apk. Keep the release entry point as is.
findings.vnote: BuildScript.cs:66 really is `options = BuildOptions.None`, and no other path in Editor/, AUTO/tools or run_autonomous.ps1 sets Development. Without a dev build there is no profiler connection, which blocks step 4 (Development APK) and capturing a freeze in the profiler. This causes no freeze itself. Extra detail for the fix: the APK path at line 58 is `HandHero_{yyyyMMdd}.apk`, so a dev build made the same day overwrites the release APK unless it gets its own suffix. Dev builds also run slower, so compare logger numbers only within the same build type.

findings.title: Every log type captures a ScriptOnly managed stack trace in the IL2CPP player
findings.frequency: per Debug.Log/LogWarning/LogError call, including engine and package logs
findings.detail: Each 01000000 is StackTraceLogType.ScriptOnly for Error, Assert, Warning, Log and Exception. On IL2CPP Android every log call walks and formats a managed stack trace and writes it to logcat (usePlayerLog 1, line 99), which can take several milliseconds per call. The game's own runtime code logs rarely: HandGestureTracker.cs:141 logs only when the subsystem report changes, and the HandProto and Core gameplay code has no per-frame or per-hit Debug.Log. The cost therefore depends on engine and package log volume, which only logcat can show. The setting is a multiplier on any log spam rather than a proven freeze cause.
findings.fix: In the release build set PlayerSettings.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Log, None) and the same for Warning, keeping ScriptOnly for Error, Exception and Assert. Do this from BuildScript so it is reproducible. During a dev-build run, check 'adb logcat -s Unity' for repeated lines; raise this finding's priority if any appear per frame or per hit.
findings.vnote: ProjectSettings.asset:57 is ScriptOnly (01000000) for all five LogTypes. That is Unity's default, not a misconfiguration. A grep of HandProto and Core finds a single Debug.Log call, HandGestureTracker.cs:141, and it is de-duplicated (only on report change). So the game's own log volume is near zero. The "several ms per call" figure is unverified. Minor correction: usePlayerLog (line 99) controls the desktop Player.log; Android always logs to logcat. Fine as a release-build cleanup, but not a freeze cause.

findings.title: OpenXR Android Latency Optimization is set to the non-default PrioritizeInputPolling
findings.code: m_latencyOptimization: 1
findings.frequency: per frame (frame-sync placement)
findings.detail: The OpenXR plugin enum has PrioritizeRendering = 0 (the documented default) and PrioritizeInputPolling = 1. Per OpenXRRenderSettings.cs:81-82, input polling priority moves xrWaitFrame to before input polling, so the main thread synchronises with the compositor earlier in the frame. My inference, not stated in the docs: this leaves less slack between simulation and submission, so a short main-thread spike more readily becomes a missed frame that the compositor reprojects, which the player sees as a freeze or stutter. It is not a freeze source on its own.
findings.fix: A/B test with the PerfSpikeLogger: one dev APK with PrioritizeRendering (0) and one with the current value, comparing spike counts over the same RUN length. Keep input polling only if aiming latency is noticeably worse without it.
findings.vnote: OpenXRPackageSettings.asset:1524 `m_latencyOptimization: 1` is inside the Android OpenXRSettings block (m_Name: Android at line 1463). The enum and remarks in OpenXRRenderSettings.cs:59-83 match the finding, and project-configuration.md:105 confirms PrioritizeRendering is the default. That less slack turns spikes into missed frames is the finder's own speculation and is not backed by the docs. The setting is not a freeze source, and only an A/B test can say more.

findings.title: HeroHealth instantiates a material per hero renderer on every RunBot spawn and never destroys it
findings.code: foreach (Renderer r in GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>()) { ... _baseColors.Add(r.material.color); }
findings.frequency: per spawn (4 materials per RunBot: Body, Nose, Fin_L, Fin_R); flash/stun recolors per hit (lines 245, 252) reuse those instances
findings.detail: Renderer.material clones the shared Lit material for each renderer. RunDirector.SpawnBot (RunDirector.cs:192) instantiates RunBot.prefab once per bot, and Horde islands respawn bots every 1.5 s with MaxAlive 2. Destroy(bot.gameObject) at RunDirector.cs:204/257 does not destroy instanced materials, and the game never calls Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets or loads a scene. These Material objects (and their per-material GPU constant buffers) therefore pile up across islands and runs, roughly tens to 100+ per run. The per-spawn clone adds CPU to the spawn frame, and RunDirector.cs:178 can spawn two bots in one frame. This is memory growth and spawn-frame cost, not a per-frame cost. PrototypeTarget.cs:20 does the same once per arena target, which is harmless.
findings.fix: Destroy the instanced materials in HeroHealth.OnDestroy (iterate _renderers, Destroy(r.material) only if an instance was created), or keep three shared materials per hero type (base, flash, stun) and swap sharedMaterial. Avoid MaterialPropertyBlock here because it takes the renderers off the SRP Batcher path. Bot pooling from the GC dimension removes the clone cost entirely.
findings.vnote: HeroHealth.cs:81 `_baseColors.Add(r.material.color)` runs in Awake. In RunBot.prefab, HeroHealth is on RunBotHero with healthBarFill = the HealthBar transform (prefab line 549). The bar is therefore skipped, and 4 renderers are cloned: Body, Nose, Fin_L and Fin_R under Visual. RunDirector.cs:192 instantiates one bot per spawn, and :204/:257 Destroy the GameObject only, so the cloned materials leak until UnloadUnusedAssets, which is never called. Horde has MaxAlive 2 (RunStateMachine.cs:50), and the :178 while-loop can spawn two bots in one frame. The cost is memory growth plus spawn-frame cost, not per frame. HandPuppeteerController.cs:82/90 also uses .material, but clutchIndicator is {fileID: 0} in the scene and the prefab, so it never runs.

findings.title: No shader/PSO warmup and shader-compile logging off; mid-RUN first-use compile is unlikely but unverified
findings.frequency: first draw of each shader-variant/render-state combination per app launch
findings.detail: Resolved shader GUIDs: Lit/Greybox/Hero/Target materials use URP Lit (933532a4...). Reticle, HealthBar, ChargeOrb, GhostHand, GroundMarker_*, MenuButton, AimCursor and BeamImpact use URP Unlit (650dd952...). Beam.mat (every LineRenderer: beam, telegraph, lock-on ring, shockwave ring, ground drop lines, menu ray) uses URP Particles/Unlit (0406db5a...). Text uses TMP Distance Field, and the sky is Skybox/Procedural. All materials are opaque with no keywords, and the build log shows small variant counts (Lit ForwardLit 128, Unlit 4, Particles/Unlit 4). Runtime code never calls Shader.Find or new Material, and crit, stun and flash only change vertex or material colors. Every combination used in RUN is already drawn in the main menu at startup: Quick Match BotHero (Lit, same materials as RunBot), reticle or cursor Unlit sphere (same as BeamImpact), ground-marker LineRenderers, and MPB menu buttons with TMP labels (same as run cards and banners). A first-use Vulkan pipeline compile mid-RUN is therefore unlikely, and it would not repeat randomly within a session. Nothing currently proves this on device.
findings.fix: In the dev APK set GraphicsSettings 'Log Shader Compilation' (m_LogWhenShaderIsCompiled: 1) and grep logcat during a RUN. If compiles appear mid-game, record a GraphicsStateCollection, or add a ShaderVariantCollection to Preloaded Shaders, and warm it up behind the main menu.
findings.vnote: GraphicsSettings.asset:40 `m_PreloadedShaders: []`, :42 `m_GraphicsStateCollection: {fileID: 0}` and :82 `m_LogWhenShaderIsCompiled: 0` are all as stated. execute.log:3188-3194 confirms URP Lit ForwardLit is 128 variants after stripping. The builder creates every material through Lit, Unlit or Particles/Unlit (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:811-824), and runtime code never creates materials. A first-use Vulkan pipeline compile mid-RUN is possible only for a state that the menu or Quick Match has not drawn. It would also be one-time per launch, because Unity's Vulkan pipeline cache usually persists across launches (from memory). So it does not explain repeating random freezes. Unproven on device.

findings.title: After any hitch, deltaTime up to 333 ms and up to 33 catch-up physics steps make a short stall look like freeze-then-jump
findings.code: Maximum Allowed Timestep: 0.33333334   (Fixed Timestep 1411199/141120000 = 0.01 s, lines 7-11; DynamicsManager.asset:22 m_AutoSyncTransforms: 1)
findings.frequency: per frame after a long frame; physics at 100 Hz every frame
findings.detail: The fixed step is 0.01 s (100 Hz, above the headset refresh), so most frames run 1-2 physics steps. After a stall, Time.deltaTime is clamped only at 0.333 s. FlyingCharacter, the bot brain and every timer then advance up to a third of a second in one frame (a hero at maxSpeed 25 m/s jumps about 8 m), and PhysX runs up to 33 steps that frame. Physics itself is cheap here: there are no Rigidbodies in Arena_Main or RunBot.prefab and no FixedUpdate in HandProto. The colliders are moved static colliders, though, and autoSyncTransforms forces a transform sync before every Raycast/OverlapSphere query (PointingBeamController.cs:402, HandMenuPointer.cs:93, ShockwaveController.cs:90). The main effect is perceptual: a stall shows up as a freeze followed by a visible jump.
findings.fix: For VR set Maximum Allowed Timestep to about 0.05-0.1 s, so the game slows down through a hitch rather than jumping. Consider Fixed Timestep 1/72, or leave 0.01 since there are no bodies. Keep autoSyncTransforms on unless queries are moved after an explicit Physics.SyncTransforms(), because raycasts against heroes moved by transform in Update rely on it.
findings.vnote: TimeManager.asset:7-12 confirms the values: fixed step 1411199/141120000 is about 0.01 s, and Maximum Allowed Timestep is 0.3333 (the Unity default). DynamicsManager.asset:22 has `m_AutoSyncTransforms: 1`. Arena_Main has 0 Rigidbody components, HandProto has no FixedUpdate, and FlyingCharacter maxSpeed is 25 (FlyingCharacter.cs:17, prefab line 526). The queries are at HandMenuPointer.cs:93, PointingBeamController.cs:402 and ShockwaveController.cs:90. The jump after a stall follows from Time.maximumDeltaTime, as its XML doc describes. The effect is on how a stall looks, not a cause, and the 100 Hz step costs little with no bodies.

findings.title: Default procedural skybox is the VR clear every frame, a constant GPU cost on Quest
findings.code: m_SkyboxMaterial: {fileID: 10304, guid: 0000000000000000f000000000000000, type: 0}   (Camera m_ClearFlags: 1 at line 8888)
findings.frequency: per frame, per eye (multiview)
findings.detail: HandHeroSceneBuilder creates the scene from NewSceneSetup.EmptyScene and never sets RenderSettings.skybox or the camera clear flags. The camera therefore clears with the built-in Skybox/Procedural (included in the build per execute.log). The arena has only a floor, a back wall and pillars, so the sky fills most of the view at render scale 1.0 with 4x MSAA. This is a steady GPU cost that reduces headroom, not a spike source.
findings.fix: In the builder, clear the VR arena to a solid color (camera.clearFlags = SolidColor) or use a cheap unlit gradient dome. ArenaViewMode already caches _arenaClearFlags in Awake, so the tabletop transparent clear keeps working.
findings.vnote: Arena_Main.unity:28 is the built-in Default-Skybox (fileID 10304, Skybox/Procedural), and line 8888 has camera `m_ClearFlags: 1`. The builder uses NewSceneSetup.EmptyScene (line 107) and never sets the skybox or clear flags. ArenaViewMode.cs:54/97 caches the clear flags as described. Correction: the sky does not fill most of the view. The arena is 35x20x35 m centred at z=20 (builder lines 34-35), so the back wall and floor cover the lower and middle field, and the sky covers roughly the upper half. URP draws the skybox after opaques, so only sky pixels are shaded. This is a steady GPU cost, not a spike.

findings.title: Fixed foveated rendering and XR performance-level hints are disabled at full render scale with 4x MSAA
findings.code:
m_Name: FoveatedRenderingFeature Android
  m_enabled: 0   (XrPerformanceSettingsFeature Android m_enabled: 0 at line 1549)
findings.frequency: per frame
findings.detail: Android uses quality level 1 (Low), which maps to 'Performance URP Config': m_MSAA 4, m_RenderScale 1 (lines 28-29), HDR off, no depth or opaque texture. That is a reasonable setup, but with FFR off every eye pixel is shaded at full rate. Without the performance-settings extension the app cannot hint CPU/GPU levels, so the runtime's dynamic clocking alone handles load changes such as two bots plus beams on an island. This means GPU headroom, not a cause of random freezes.
findings.fix: Enable the OpenXR Foveated Rendering feature for Android (Meta FFR, medium level) and test it. Optionally enable XrPerformanceSettingsFeature and request a sustained-high CPU level while an island is fought. Measure both with the logger's GPU time (RS-1).
findings.vnote: OpenXRPackageSettings.asset:2194 (FoveatedRenderingFeature Android) and :1549 (XrPerformanceSettingsFeature Android) both have `m_enabled: 0`. QualitySettings sets Android to level 1, which uses Performance URP Config (guid fd42a132), and lines 28-29 are MSAA 4 and RenderScale 1. That config also has 4096 soft main-light shadows (lines 45-46), but the only light has `m_Shadows.m_Type: 0` (Arena_Main.unity:1700), so no shadow pass runs. The scene is light: 1 camera, 1 light, 81 mesh renderers, 11 LineRenderers. GPU headroom therefore looks unlikely to cause random freezes. The fix needs more than ticking the feature: FFR also needs XRDisplaySubsystem.foveatedRenderingLevel (or the SRP foveation API) set at runtime.

findings.title: URP volume framework updates every frame although post-processing cannot run
findings.code: m_VolumeFrameworkUpdateMode: 0
findings.frequency: per frame
findings.detail: The update mode is EveryFrame, and the URP global settings point at DefaultVolumeProfile.asset, which has about 19 active overrides (Bloom, Tonemapping, DOF, MotionBlur and others). The Android renderer has no PostProcessData (Android Preset.asset:31 postProcessData: {fileID: 0}), and the runtime-added camera data defaults to post-processing off, so none of this is ever rendered. VolumeManager still re-evaluates the stack for the XR camera each frame. The cost is small but wasted main-thread time.
findings.fix: Set Volume Update Mode to 'Via Scripting' on Performance URP Config (and on the camera if added). Optionally clear the default volume profile's overrides.
findings.vnote: Performance URP Config.asset:94 is `m_VolumeFrameworkUpdateMode: 0` (EveryFrame). Android Preset.asset:31 is `postProcessData: {fileID: 0}`. The global settings point at Assets/DefaultVolumeProfile.asset, which has about 19 components. URP UniversalRenderPipeline.cs:1416-1461 really calls ResetMainStack plus VolumeManager.Update every frame in this mode. This wastes some main-thread time per frame but is not a spike source.

findings.title: Use OpenXR Predicted Time is off for Android
findings.code: m_useOpenXRPredictedTime: 0
findings.frequency: per frame
findings.detail: The OpenXR settings reference says enabling it gives smoother rendering by synchronising with the runtime's predicted display time, and Unity recommends it on headsets. With it off, frame timing follows Unity's own clock, so frame-time jitter feeds directly into Time.deltaTime-driven motion (heroes, beams, rings). This affects smoothness and is not a stall source. I have not verified how it interacts with the long-frame clamp in RS-7.
findings.fix: Enable it in a test dev APK and compare spike and jitter logs against the current build.
findings.vnote: OpenXRPackageSettings.asset:1536 `m_useOpenXRPredictedTime: 0` is in the Android block. The code default is true (OpenXRRenderSettings.cs:495), so this is a non-default value. Mechanism correction: the tooltip and settings-reference.md:34 describe the setting as the runtime predicting display presentation time for poses and rendering sync. Nothing in the docs ties it to Time.deltaTime, so that part of the finding is unverified. It is not a stall source.

findings.title: HandGestureTracker allocates every frame (new List + string.Join) while no hand subsystem is running
findings.frequency: per frame, only while _subsystem is null or not running (before XR init, after an OpenXR session stop/resume such as headset sleep); never while hands are merely untracked
findings.detail: Update calls FindSubsystem every frame until a running XRHandSubsystem exists. Each call allocates a new List, a parts List, per-subsystem interpolated strings and a joined report, and only the Debug.Log is de-duplicated. During normal play the subsystem keeps running, because losing a hand only flips hand.isTracked, so this is not a mid-island source. After a resume from sleep or the system menu, though, it produces a burst of garbage on the frames when GC pressure matters most. Nothing here starts or stops subsystems or blocks the main thread.
findings.fix: Reuse a static List<XRHandSubsystem>, retry FindSubsystem at most every 0.5-1 s (unscaled), and build the report string only when the subsystem count or running flags change.
findings.vnote: HandGestureTracker.cs:88-90 calls FindSubsystem only while `_subsystem == null || !_subsystem.running`. The allocations are at :110 (new List), :133 (parts list), :135 (interpolated string) and :136 (string.Join). Hand loss alone only sets IsTracked=false at :146-151 and does not trigger this. The frequency is therefore correct: per frame only before XR init or after a subsystem stop, never mid-island while the subsystem is running. Strictly this is a GC-dimension finding.

findings.title: 27 TMP labels and headers have no serialized font and all use auto-size; run panels first lay out mid-run
findings.code: m_fontAsset: {fileID: 0}   (27 of 31 TextMeshPro components; builder: HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:761 AddComponent<TextMeshPro>() under panels made inactive at :525, label.enableAutoSizing = true at :563)
findings.frequency: per event: first activation of each run panel (portal, chest, shop) per launch; re-layout of 4 shop slots + REROLL on every buy/reroll (RunChoiceMenu.cs:110-120)
findings.detail: The panels are SetActive(false) before their buttons are added, so TMP's editor Awake never ran and no font was serialized. On first activation on device, TextMeshPro.LoadFontAsset assigns TMP_Settings.defaultFontAsset and calls m_sharedMaterial.SetFloat("_CullMode", 0) on the shared font material, then builds the mesh. Every Label and Header has enableAutoSizing, which runs TMP's iterative fit, and the chest and shop cards also wrap multi-line rich text. On Quest this is likely a few milliseconds per panel show, an estimate not measured on device. The text is all ASCII, which LiberationSans SDF (static atlas) covers, so the dynamic fallback font never rasterizes glyphs at runtime.
findings.fix: In HandHeroSceneBuilder.WorldText set text.font = TMP_Settings.defaultFontAsset (and fontSharedMaterial) explicitly, and pre-activate and deactivate the run panels once behind the main menu. Consider fixed font sizes instead of auto-size for cards.
findings.vnote: 27 of the 31 TMP components in Arena_Main have `m_fontAsset: {fileID: 0}`. Line 595 itself is the pause panel's RESUME label, not a run panel. The builder makes panels inactive at :525 before WorldText's AddComponent at :761, and sets auto-size at :563/:580. TextMeshPro.cs:936-956 confirms LoadFontAsset uses TMP_Settings.defaultFontAsset and calls SetFloat("_CullMode", 0) when no font is set. LiberationSans SDF is static (m_AtlasPopulationMode: 0), so no glyph rasterization happens. The run panels first activate in ChoosePortal, OpenChest or Shop (RunChoiceMenu.cs:102-104), which come between islands, not during combat. The few-ms cost is unmeasured.

findings.title: Synchronous PlayerPrefs.Save on menu/tutorial events (verified never per frame)
findings.code:
PlayerPrefs.SetInt(TutorialSeenKey, 1);
PlayerPrefs.Save();
findings.frequency: per event: tutorial complete/skip (the frame a first-ever RUN starts after the tutorial); AimModeSetting.cs:38 and ArenaViewMode.cs:67 on main-menu toggles
findings.detail: On Android, PlayerPrefs.Save writes the preferences file synchronously on the main thread. It never runs per frame or during an island, so it cannot explain random freezes mid-run. It can add a small one-off hitch at the tutorial-to-RUN transition. No other runtime file IO, Resources.Load, GC.Collect, Thread.Sleep, targetFrameRate or QualitySettings change exists in HandProto or Core.
findings.fix: Leave as is, or defer the Save to the next menu return or OnApplicationPause. PerfSpikeLogger's own file writes must likewise be buffered and flushed only on pause or quit (or off the main thread), or the logger will create the spikes it is measuring.
findings.vnote: MatchDirector.cs:99-100 (CompleteTutorial), AimModeSetting.cs:37-38 (menu toggle) and ArenaViewMode.cs:66-67 call PlayerPrefs.Save. ArenaViewMode returns early unless rememberChoice is set (default false, line 40). All three run per event, never per frame or during an island. Grep finds no other File, Resources, GC.Collect or targetFrameRate use in HandProto or Core. The advice about buffering PerfSpikeLogger writes is correct and important.

findings.title: Focus-loss and user-presence auto-pause freeze game time with no log trail, so they cannot be told apart from a stall
findings.code: if (!hasFocus && pauseOnFocusLoss) Pause();   /   if (_userWasPresent && !present) Pause();  (line 211) -> Time.timeScale = paused ? 0f : 1f; (line 231)
findings.frequency: per event: OS focus loss (system menu or overlay, Meta right-palm pinch gesture), proximity-sensor present->absent edge (polled per frame at line 207)
findings.detail: When either fires, the whole arena stops (timeScale 0) while head tracking keeps rendering. A PAUSED banner and panel do appear, so this is probably not the reported symptom. Proximity-sensor flicker or a brief system overlay would still look like the game froze, and right now nothing records it. The per-frame XRInputDevices query reuses _heads and is cheap. The Input System runs in dynamic update by default (no custom InputSettings asset), so timeScale 0 does not stall head pose.
findings.fix: Have PerfSpikeLogger also append a line (with preallocated buffers) on OnApplicationFocus, OnApplicationPause, MatchDirector.PausedChanged and userPresence transitions, so every 'freeze' report can be matched against a spike or a pause.
findings.vnote: MatchDirector.cs:156 (focus), :161 (pause), :207-211 (per-frame userPresence poll with a reused _heads list) and :231 (Time.timeScale = 0) are as quoted. MatchHud.cs:43 shows a PAUSED banner, so an auto-pause is visible and is probably not the reported symptom. Logging these transitions in PerfSpikeLogger is cheap and helps tell a pause apart from a stall. Whether proximity flicker or system gestures actually fire mid-run is unverified.

missed.title: Android OpenXR Depth Submission Mode is None: missed frames can only be reprojected without depth
missed.frequency: per frame (affects how the compositor shows every missed or late frame)
missed.detail: Line 1528 is in the Android OpenXRSettings block (m_Name: Android at line 1463). The OpenXR package docs (Documentation~/project-configuration.md:203-217) say None means no depth-based stability or reprojection support from the platform is enabled. They also say depth can significantly reduce judder, and they recommend 16-bit depth on battery-powered headsets unless the cost outweighs the benefit. When the app misses frames, the Quest compositor then re-shows the last frame without depth-aware correction. Any hitch is therefore more visible as the world sticking or juddering. This does not cause stalls. It only affects how visible a stall is, and depth submission adds some bandwidth cost.
missed.fix: In one dev APK set Depth Submission Mode to Depth 16 bit (OpenXRSettings.depthSubmissionMode, from BuildScript so it is reproducible). A/B it against the current build, comparing perceived freezes and the logger's spike counts and GPU time. Keep it only if the judder improves without a GPU cost regression.

dimensions.notes:
Scope: I read every file under HandProto completely, plus the Core state machines and input helpers they depend on, and the scene builder wiring (lines 100-719). All analysis is static; nothing was run.

How the six known minors check out (from AUTO/REPORT_FOR_HYUN.md §7):
- Known (1) is BR-4. The code is present. The stated trigger (death on the focus-loss frame) is closed by synchronous input gating. The real trigger is a bot beam landing in the frame a Horde island clears. The suggested fix needs the any-phase death handling, otherwise it can softlock.
- Known (2) is BR-5. Present; the fix is correct when combined with BR-4.
- Known (3) is BR-8. The code is present but unreachable now.
- Known (4) is BR-6. Present; I proposed a concrete team filter.
- Known (5) is BR-10. Present; the fix is right. Correction: the throw happens on press, not in Awake.
- Known (6) is BR-9. Present and cosmetic; fix by ending the run synchronously on PhaseChanged.

Checked and found OK:
- Event subscriptions: every += has a matching -= or a shared lifetime. This covers HeroHealth.hitReceiver, BotInputSource.hitReceiver, PointingBeamController.health.Respawned, MatchDirector and RunDirector Died, TutorialDirector target.Hit, and the per-bot Died closures, which die with the bot.
- Coroutines: none exist. The only deferred call is PrototypeTarget.Invoke (greybox targets).
- Time.timeScale: written only by MatchDirector.OnPausedChanged and OnDisable. ReturnToMenu always unpauses.
- Destroyed-bot references: the AimAssistTarget registry deregisters in OnDisable. PointingBeamController drops dead or inactive targets through IsTargetable. LockOnRing hides on a Unity-null target. BotTelegraphLine and its renderers are destroyed with the bot root.
- Island clear: cannot fire twice.
- Deaths: are not double-processed (the model ignores hits on the dead, and OnBotDied removes the bot from the list first).
- Choice panels: double picks are prevented by the phase change, armDelay on unscaled time, and the pointer's rising-edge pinch with _waitForOpenHand.
- Input buffer after pause or menu: ShotCooldown's pending shot is cleared by HasAim = false when input is off, and pinch/trigger RequireReopen runs on enable. The gaps are the clutch and push state (BR-2).
- State between runs: RunStateMachine.StartRun and ReturnToMenu, RunHeroStats.Bind, ResetHealth and the Intro handler reset everything that matters. _nextSpawnPoint is not reset, which is cosmetic.

Not reported as findings (low value or unreachable):
- RunDirector.BuyShopItem and RerollShop (RunDirector.cs:90-91) skip the match-level !Paused check that the other choice methods have. Only a press in the same frame as the pause would get through.
- PortalRoller.Roll can return 0 portals if every chest pool is empty. RunChoiceMenu then shows no buttons, a softlock, but that is practically unreachable within one run's 8 chests and the shop.
- BotBrain.Reset sets _fireTimer from params captured before SetFireIntervalScale, so the boss's first shot uses the base interval. Trivial.

Relevance to the reported 'random freeze': none of these correctness bugs freezes the rendered image. Stuck-looking states are limited to:
- the potential softlock if the known-minor fix is applied naively (BR-4);
- auto-pause from focus loss or the proximity sensor (MatchDirector.cs:154-162, 204-213). This sets timeScale 0, but shows a PAUSED banner and the pause panel; worth asking Hyun whether a 'freeze' ever showed PAUSED.

For the perf dimension (outside my scope but freeze-relevant): HandGestureTracker.Update calls FindSubsystem every frame while the hand subsystem is not running (HandGestureTracker.cs:88-99, 107-142). Each call allocates a new List, GetSubsystems and report strings (string.Join and interpolation), so it produces per-frame garbage whenever hand tracking is stopped, for example while controllers are in use or around focus changes.

findings.title: A run revive teleports the hero to spawn, then the clutch spring pulls it straight back to where it died
findings.code:
public void Revive(float health) { _model.Reset(); _model.SetHealth(health); Respawn(); }   // called from RunDirector.cs:211 inside the Died event
// HandPuppeteerController.cs:58  if (!character.IsAlive) { if (_clutch.IsClutched) OnRelease(); _clutch.Reset(); return; }
findings.frequency: per revive (RUN with a Revives item)
findings.detail: HeroHealth.Die() -> Died -> RunDirector.OnPlayerDied -> playerHealth.Revive() all run in one call stack inside the bot's beam hit, so FlyingCharacter goes dead and alive again before any other Update runs. HandPuppeteerController only drops its ClutchMapper when it polls character.IsAlive == false (line 58), so it never sees the death. FlyingCharacter.Respawn (FlyingCharacter.cs:89-97) clears _hasTarget and moves the hero to the spawn point. On the next frame the player's fist is usually still closed, because they were flying when hit, so XRHandsInputSource still reports ClutchHeld. ClutchMapper.Step (ClutchMapper.cs:47-52) keeps its old _target and the puppeteer calls character.SetTarget(old target) (HandPuppeteerController.cs:72-76). The revived hero then springs back toward the spot where it died, at up to maxSpeed. That undoes the 'alive again at the spawn point' safety of the revive. The same missed death also leaves a pending buffered shot or an active charge on PointingBeamController, so it can fire right after the revive.
findings.fix: Make respawns observable to the controllers. Option 1: add a spawn counter or a Respawned event on FlyingCharacter, incremented in Respawn(); HandPuppeteerController calls _clutch.Reset() (and OnRelease) when it changes, and PointingBeamController cancels its charge and pending shot. Option 2: have HandPuppeteerController subscribe to HeroHealth.Respawned the way PointingBeamController does (PointingBeamController.cs:132). Either way a still-closed fist then regrabs from the spawn point with zero delta.
findings.vnote: Verified the chain. In HeroHealth.ApplyDamage (104), Die() calls character.Kill(), then the Died event. RunDirector.OnPlayerDied (208-212) calls playerHealth.Revive (132-137), which runs Respawn() and FlyingCharacter.Respawn (89-97, _alive=true, _hasTarget=false). All of this happens inside the bot's PointingBeamController.Fire -> BeamHitReceiver.Receive. HandPuppeteerController only resets its ClutchMapper when it sees !character.IsAlive (58-62), so it never sees the death. ClutchMapper.Step (47-52) keeps its old _target and adds deltas, and line 76 calls SetTarget, so the hero springs back toward the old clutch target. That target is roughly where the hero was flying, not exactly where it died. The code at 56-57 explicitly states the opposite intent. The charge and pending-shot part is also real: ChargeInputRule.Decide and ClearPending (223) only check IsAlive, which is true again. Frequency: every revive while the left fist is held, which is normal while flying. It needs a Revives item, so it is rare per run but deterministic when it happens.

findings.title: Re-enabling XRHandsInputSource reuses stale clutch and palm-push state: hero or cursor jumps, and a spurious shockwave can fire at island start, round start and resume
findings.frequency: per input re-enable: every RUN island start, every resume from pause, every Quick Match Fight start
findings.detail: MatchDirector and RunDirector switch the player's input off between fights and while paused (SetEnabled(fightOnly) / SetRunControls). While the source is off, Sample() is not called, so _clutch, _aimClutch, _leftPush and _rightPush keep the state of the last enabled frame. OnEnable resets only the pinch and the trigger. (1) Clutch: if the left fist was closed when input went off (likely, since the player is flying when the island clears or focus is lost), HandClutchSampler's gate stays on. On the first frame back, with the fist still >= releaseThreshold 0.45, there is no Rising edge, so delta = palmNow - palmAtDisable (HandClutchSampler.cs:26-33), a gap of seconds of hand movement. Meanwhile HandPuppeteerController's ClutchMapper was released, because Current was default while disabled. It grabs on this frame, and ClutchMapper.Step adds the delta on the grab frame itself (ClutchMapper.cs:35-52). Result: target = hero + stale delta x 60 (positionScale), so 10 cm of hand drift becomes about a 6 m lurch at FIGHT. Players who close the fist during the Intro countdown to be ready hit this. The CURSOR aim marker jumps the same way through _aimClutch / AimClutchDelta. (2) Palm push: PalmPushRecognizer keeps _hasLast and _lastPosition (GestureRecognizers.cs:76-88). The first sample after re-enable divides the whole gap's displacement by one frame's dt. About 1.7 cm along the palm normal at 72 Hz already exceeds PushSpeed 1.2 m/s, so an open hand that moved fires a shockwave on the first fighting frame. That puts the 3 s cooldown on the player's real shockwave, and on resume mid-fight it gives a free stun.
findings.fix: Add Reset() to HandClutchSampler (gate.Reset()), PalmPushRecognizer (gate.Reset(), _hasLast = false) and PalmsTogetherRecognizer, and call them for _clutch, _aimClutch, _leftPush, _rightPush and _palmsTogether in XRHandsInputSource.OnEnable (or OnDisable). A still-closed fist then gives a Rising edge with zero delta: a regrab from where the hero is, as ClutchMapper intends. Add a Core EditMode test: Step with fist on, a gap without Step, Reset, Step again, and expect delta == 0.
findings.vnote: Verified. In Arena_Main, fightOnly contains only xrInput (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:233). While it is disabled, Sample() does not run, and OnEnable (70-74) resets only _pinch and _trigger. HandClutchSampler (26-33): if the gate was on, there is no Rising edge while the fist is >=0.45, so delta = palmNow - stale _lastPalmPosition. ClutchMapper adds the delta on the grab frame (35-52); AimCursorModelTests.Reset_WhileHeld_RegrabsFromNewPosition (81-90) even asserts this. PalmPushRecognizer (76-89) keeps _hasLast/_lastPosition, so the whole gap's displacement is divided by one dt. Correction on frequency: the hero/cursor lurch only happens if the clutch gate was ON at the disable moment (for example an island cleared mid-flight) AND the fist is still >=0.45 on the first enabled frame. 'Closing the fist during the countdown' alone is not enough when the gate was off at disable, because that gives a clean Rising edge with zero delta. The palm-push variant is probably the more frequent one. Either open hand (fist <=0.35) that moved more than ~1.7 cm along its palm normal since the last fight frame fires a shockwave ring and puts the 3 s cooldown on it. That is roughly half of the island starts where the hands are open, since the right hand moves a lot picking chest and portal cards. Player-visible, not a headset freeze.

findings.title: After hand-tracking loss, HandGestureTracker smooths from the stale pose, so the clutch drags the hero and fake palm pushes fire
findings.frequency: per hand-tracking reacquire (common on Quest with fists and at the edge of the field of view)
findings.detail: UpdateHand keeps the last pose while untracked (lines 146-152). When the hand comes back, position, rotation and the strengths are lerped from that stale value, about 29 % per frame at 72 Hz, instead of snapping. Downstream code assumes the reacquired sample is a fresh pose. HandClutchSampler resets on tracking loss and, on reacquire with a fist, sets _lastPalmPosition to the first smoothed sample. The following frames then report the remaining catch-up of about 0.71 x D as clutch deltas, so the hero moves about 0.71 x D x 60 (10 cm of hand offset is about 4 m, 30 cm is about 13 m). That contradicts the stated intent in XRHandsInputSource.cs:86-87 ('glides instead of teleporting when the hand comes back somewhere else'). PalmPushRecognizer also resets _hasLast on loss 'so the jump is never read as speed' (GestureRecognizers.cs:68-73). The smoothed slide over the next frames is still read as speed: the second frame moves about 0.21 x D, so roughly 8 cm of offset along the palm normal already gives more than 1.2 m/s and a spurious shockwave. A stale FistStrength can also cause a 1-2 frame grab on an open hand.
findings.fix: Track the previous IsTracked per hand. On the untracked -> tracked frame, snap PalmPosition, TrackingPalmPosition, PalmRotation, the strengths and the AimRay direction to the raw values (posT = valT = 1), and smooth only from the second tracked frame on.
findings.vnote: Code verified. UpdateHand keeps the stale pose while untracked (146-152) and lerps from it on reacquire (167-172; posT ~0.29 at 72 Hz, valT ~0.22). HandClutchSampler resets on loss, so the Rising frame anchors _lastPalmPosition to the first smoothed sample, and the remaining ~0.71*D arrives as clutch deltas (x60). The PalmPushRecognizer second-frame speed is about 0.21*D/dt, so D_normal >= ~8 cm exceeds 1.2 m/s. The math holds. A stale FistStrength of 1.0 gives 0.78 on the first frame, which is a grab on an open hand for about 3 frames. Impact is speculative. For brief losses mid-motion, the catch-up points in the direction the hand was already moving, which may look intended. The bad case is a long loss where the hand comes back somewhere else with a fist. How often fist tracking loss happens is a device fact I could not verify here.

findings.title: Known minor (1): an ignored player death gives a free full heal. It is still present, the stated trigger is not the reachable one, and the suggested fix as written would softlock
findings.frequency: rare: per Horde clear (or Victory/Defeat) where a remaining bot's beam lands in the same frame
findings.detail: The code is still present: RunDirector.cs:208-212 plus RunStateMachine.cs:217. An ignored death is then auto-respawned by HeroHealth.Update (HeroHealth.cs:172), and HeroHealthModel.Tick resets to full MaxHealth after 3 s (HeroHealthModel.cs:140-144). The trigger in the report ('death on the same frame as focus loss') is effectively closed with the current wiring. A match pause disables the player input synchronously (MatchDirector.OnPausedChanged -> ApplyControlGating, lines 229-242). The run only becomes paused inside RunDirector.Update, which disables every bot in the same call (SyncPause at 113, ApplyControls at 118 -> RunBot.SetControlled -> OnDisable zeroes Current). So nothing can deal damage while _run.IsPaused. The reachable trigger is the Phase != Island branch. On a Horde clear, RunDirector.Update -> Tick -> ClearIsland -> DespawnBots calls Destroy, which is deferred to the end of the frame, and clears _bots, so ApplyControls loops an empty list and never disables the doomed bots. A bot whose PointingBeamController has not run yet this frame still holds input sampled at order -50 and can fire. If that kills the player, the death is ignored (IslandCleared). The player then also skips the spiked-chest cost (line 233, !IsDead) and respawns at full health. This relies on Unity still updating objects that were Destroy()ed earlier in the same frame, which I believe it does but have not verified on device. On the suggested fix ('turn off auto-respawn during the run, process the death regardless of pause'): the direction is right but it is incomplete. With auto-respawn off, the Phase != Island early return leaves the hero dead for good. ReturnToSpawn skips dead heroes (HeroHealth.cs:142), bots see no living enemy (BotInputSource.cs:77), and an Arena/Elite/Boss island can never clear. The player sees an invisible hero and idle bots, a softlock that could pass for a freeze, until MENU.
findings.fix: (a) In DespawnBots, call bot.SetControlled(false) and bot.gameObject.SetActive(false) before Destroy, so despawned bots stop updating, lose their colliders and leave the AimAssist registry immediately. (b) If auto-respawn is turned off in the run (a flag on HeroHealth set in BeginRun and cleared in EndRun), OnPlayerDied must resolve a death in every non-Idle run phase: revive or Defeat outside Island too, or at least revive at the next Intro. (c) Drop the IsPaused gate in RunStateMachine.ReportPlayerDeath (safe: a Defeat while paused just waits for RESUME). Add an EditMode test for 'death outside Island is never left unresolved'.
findings.vnote: Code present: RunDirector.cs:210 and RunStateMachine.cs:217, then auto-respawn at HeroHealth.cs:172 with full health (HeroHealthModel.Tick 140-144). Agreed that the IsPaused branch is unreachable: the match pause disables the player input synchronously, and the bots are disabled in the same RunDirector.Update that pauses _run (113-118). Correction on the trigger: only a Horde clear can do this. On an Arena, Elite or Boss clear every bot is already dead, and dead bots cannot fire (ChargeInputRule/ClearPending check IsAlive). Victory follows a boss clear with no bots, and Defeat means the player is already dead. The mechanism is real: DespawnBots calls Destroy, which is deferred, then _bots.Clear(), so ApplyControls never disables the doomed bots. A bot PointingBeamController ordered after RunDirector can still fire from its order -50 Current. This assumes Unity still updates Destroy()-marked objects for the rest of the frame (widely observed, not verified here). The probability per clear is tiny: a lethal hit on one exact frame. The chest-skip detail checks out: ClearedTime 2 s < RespawnDelay 3 s. The softlock critique of the suggested fix is logically correct (ReturnToSpawn 142, BotInputSource 77).

findings.title: Known minor (2): after DEFEAT the hero auto-respawns and shows behind the end screen (still present; the suggested fix works only with the BR-4 caveats)
findings.code:
if (_model.Tick(Time.deltaTime)) Respawn();
// RunDirector.cs:237-241: case RunPhase.Victory: case RunPhase.Defeat: DespawnBots(); if (match != null) match.SetRunControls(false); break;
findings.frequency: per Defeat (3 s after it, while the end panel is up)
findings.detail: Defeat leaves the HeroHealthModel dead with _respawnTimer = 3 s (HeroHealthModel.cs:101-103). Nothing in RunDirector stops it, and game time keeps running on the end screen. After 3 s Respawn() moves the hero to the spawn point, re-enables its renderers and colliders (SetVisible(true)) and fires Respawned, so the hero reappears at the arena center behind the DEFEAT banner and MENU panel. Controls stay off (SetRunControls(false)), so the effect is visual only. The suggested fix (auto-respawn off during the run, same as (1)) is correct for this case. EndRun already calls ResetHealth (RunDirector.cs:250) and MatchDirector resets on Menu (MatchDirector.cs:222), so the hero comes back when leaving the screen. It must be combined with the any-phase death handling from BR-4, or it creates the permanent-death softlock.
findings.fix: Add HeroHealth.SetAutoRespawn(bool) (or HeroHealthModel.AutoRespawn), set to false in RunDirector.BeginRun and true in EndRun, and keep explicit Revive/ResetHealth as the only way back during a run. Apply together with BR-4 (b).
findings.vnote: Verified. A Defeat leaves the model dead with _respawnTimer = 3 s (HeroHealthModel 101-103). RunDirector's Defeat case (237-241) does nothing to health. Time is not paused, so HeroHealth.Update:172 calls Respawn(): SetVisible(true), hero at its spawn, Respawned fires. The end panel stays up because HandMenu runOver is true. Visual only, since controls are off. The fix note is right that it must be paired with any-phase death handling.

findings.title: Known minor (4): bots' beams damage other bots, those kills pay the player, and the friendly hit triggers a dodge
findings.frequency: per bot shot on islands with 2 bots alive (Arena 3+, Horde)
findings.detail: This is still present. A bot's Fire ray goes from its hero to its aim point and stops at the first collider that is not its own hero (RaycastIgnoringSelf, lines 399-415). A second bot in between takes the hit. In addition, the bot's smoothed _rawAimPoint can itself land on the other bot (UpdateAim at line 266). HeroHealth.OnBeamHit ignores BeamHit.Shooter (HeroHealth.cs:163-166), and the Elite damage multiplier applies too. The kill reaches RunDirector through the per-bot Died closure (RunDirector.cs:195) -> OnBotDied -> _run.ReportBotKilled(), which adds crystals and a kill and can clear the island without the player firing. BotInputSource.OnHit (BotInputSource.cs:60-63) also starts an evade on a friendly hit. The final report only says to tidy this up and gives no concrete fix.
findings.fix: Filter by team in the beam, not in the health. In RaycastIgnoringSelf, skip colliders whose hero is on the shooter's team: for example a team id on FlyingCharacter or AimAssistTarget, set to Bot on the RunBot prefab and on the Quick Match bot. Bot beams then pass through teammates and neither damage nor dodge happens. Quick Match is unaffected (one bot). As a backstop, ignore hits in HeroHealth.OnBeamHit when hit.Shooter is on the same team.
findings.vnote: Verified. RaycastIgnoringSelf (399-415) skips only the shooter's own hero. Fire (359-368) delivers the hit to the first other hero, and HeroHealth.OnBeamHit (163-166) ignores the Shooter. A friendly kill goes through the Died closure (RunDirector:195) -> ReportBotKilled, which pays crystals and can clear the island. BotInputSource.OnHit (60-63) triggers an evade. Corrections: RunBot.prefab has assistAngle: 0, so bots never aim-snap onto each other. The friendly hit only happens when a bot is physically in the ray (UpdateAim raycast at 266 or the Fire ray). Elite islands spawn exactly one bot (RunRules.Island leaves BotCount = MaxAlive = 1), so the 'Elite multiplier applies too' remark is moot. Applies to Arena 3+ and Horde. Frequency depends on geometry: occasional.

findings.title: Bots spawned in the same frame get the same RNG seed and fire in lockstep
findings.code: _brain = new BotBrain(CurrentParams(), seed != 0 ? seed : System.Environment.TickCount);
findings.frequency: per island start with MaxAlive 2 (Arena islands 3+, Horde): both bots spawn in one frame via `while (_run.WantsSpawn(_bots.Count) && SpawnBot()) { }` (RunDirector.cs:178)
findings.detail: The RunBot prefab and scene have seed: 0 (RunBot.prefab:898), so each bot seeds from Environment.TickCount, which has millisecond resolution. Two Instantiate calls in the same frame almost always land in the same millisecond, so both BotBrains share one System.Random stream. Both also start with _fireTimer = FireInterval when enabled in the same frame (BotBrain.cs:136), and every later interval uses the same jitter draw (BotBrain.cs:276/287). Both bots therefore telegraph and fire on the same frames, and flip strafe on the same timers, until a hit makes one of them draw extra numbers in StartEvade. The comment's intent ('0 = different every play') is not met. In practice the player faces paired simultaneous red lines instead of staggered ones.
findings.fix: Derive a unique seed per spawn. Either RunDirector passes one from its own _rng through RunBot.Setup, or BotInputSource mixes in a static counter: `seed != 0 ? seed : Environment.TickCount ^ (++s_spawnCounter * 7919)`. Optionally stagger the first shot: _fireTimer = FireInterval + rng * jitter in Reset.
findings.vnote: Code verified. RunBot.prefab:898 has seed: 0. The prefab's BotInputSource is m_Enabled: 0 (line 888), but Awake still runs inside Instantiate because the GameObject is active, so two spawns in the same frame read Environment.TickCount (ms resolution) usually in the same ms. That the seeds match is likely but not verified on device. Corrections: (1) The first shot is simultaneous regardless of seed. BotBrain.Reset sets _fireTimer = FireInterval with no jitter (136), and both bots are enabled the same frame, so staggering the first shot matters more than the seed. (2) Lockstep does not last 'until a hit'. The rng streams diverge as soon as the bots take different FlipStrafe draws (only in Strafe state, or a wall-pin flip at 256), which their different spawn distances make likely. Only the Horde start and Arena 3+ starts spawn 2 bots in one frame.

findings.title: Known minor (3): kills during a paused frame are dropped. The code is present but not reachable with the current gating
findings.frequency: would be per kill while _run.IsPaused; currently unreachable
findings.detail: The guard is still there: the bot is removed and destroyed, but ReportBotKilled returns false while the run is paused, so crystals and the kill count are lost. On Arena islands a replacement then spawns, because _islandKills + alive < BotCount, so progress is not blocked. However, nothing can kill a bot while _run.IsPaused. The player's input is switched off synchronously when the match pauses (MatchDirector.cs:229-242), before the run pauses, and the run pause and the bot disable happen in the same RunDirector.Update (lines 113-118). A kill landing between the match pause and SyncPause is still counted, because _run is not paused yet. So this is a latent hazard only.
findings.fix: Optional hardening: count a kill whenever _bots.Remove(bot) succeeds by dropping the IsPaused check in ReportBotKilled. A clear while paused just waits, since Tick is frozen. Keep the Phase == Island check.
findings.vnote: The code is present: RunDirector 202-205 and RunStateMachine:198. I agree it is unreachable today. Player input is cut synchronously at the match pause (MatchDirector 229-242). Bots are disabled in the same RunDirector.Update that sets _run.IsPaused, and BotInputSource.OnDisable zeroes Current. Kills between the match pause and SyncPause are counted because _run is not paused yet. Latent hazard only, no runtime effect.

findings.title: Known minor (6): returning to MENU resets health with run items still bound; RunDirector ends the run one Update late by polling
findings.frequency: per return to MENU from a run
findings.detail: This is still present. MatchStateMachine.ReturnToMenu -> OnPhaseChanged(Menu) -> playerHealth.ResetHealth(), whose SyncMaxHealth still reads the bound RunHeroStats and so sets the item-boosted max. RunDirector only notices the phase change when its Update polls match.Match.Phase (RunDirector.cs:107-111). EndRun then unbinds and resets again (lines 245-252), in the same frame or the next depending on script order. The visible effect is nil, since the hero bar is normalized and the HUD score line is hidden in Menu. The same lag also delays DespawnBots, unhiding the Quick Match bot (SetHidden(false)) and _run.ReturnToMenu by up to one frame. The report suggests no fix.
findings.fix: Subscribe RunDirector to match.Match.PhaseChanged (in Start, after MatchDirector.Awake has created _match) and call EndRun synchronously when the phase leaves Run while IsRunning. MatchDirector's handler runs first, but EndRun re-resets in the same call stack, so no frame shows the stale state. Keep the Update check as a fallback.
findings.vnote: Verified. MatchStateMachine.ReturnToMenu -> PhaseChanged(Menu) -> MatchDirector.OnPhaseChanged:222 calls ResetHealth while RunHeroStats is still bound. RunDirector notices only in its next Update poll (107-111) and then calls EndRun (unbind + reset). No visible effect: in Menu, MatchHud hides the score line and the banner shows the title. During the lag frame the bots may still be enabled, but a death then is harmless because EndRun resets right after. Correct as described.

findings.title: Known minor (5): RunChoiceMenu.Awake binds method groups on 'run', which throws when 'run' is a real null (player build)
findings.code:
if (rerollButton != null) rerollButton.SetCustomAction(() => Choose(run.RerollShop));
if (leaveButton != null) leaveButton.SetCustomAction(() => Choose(run.LeaveShop));
findings.frequency: would be per button press (inside the lambda), only if 'run' is unassigned
findings.detail: This is still present. Correction to the report: the method-group delegate is created inside the outer lambda, so Awake itself does not throw. The exception comes later, on a press of REROLL or LEAVE, because creating a delegate from an instance method on a null receiver throws, and this happens before Choose's own `run == null` guard runs. In the Editor an unassigned serialized reference is a non-null 'fake null' object, so the problem may not reproduce there. The scene builder always wires 'run' (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:621), so it is unreachable today. The suggested fix `Choose(() => run.RerollShop())` is correct: the dereference then happens inside Choose's guarded call.
findings.fix: Use lambdas: `Choose(() => run.RerollShop())` and `Choose(() => run.LeaveShop())`.
findings.vnote: Code at RunChoiceMenu.cs:82-83. The finder's own correction is right: the method-group conversion runs inside the outer lambda at press time, before Choose's run==null guard. In the Editor the fake-null object avoids it. In a player build, whether creating a delegate for a non-virtual method on a null target throws (ArgumentException/NRE) under IL2CPP is uncertain; if it doesn't throw, Choose's guard returns safely. Unreachable anyway: Arena_Main.unity:5056 wires run, as does HandHeroSceneBuilder:621. The lambda fix is correct and trivial.

findings.title: Every RunBot spawn leaks about 4 Material instances (renderer.material in HeroHealth.Awake, never destroyed)
findings.code:
_renderers.Add(r);
_baseColors.Add(r.material.color);
findings.frequency: per bot spawn (RunDirector.cs:192); flashes reuse the same instances
findings.detail: Renderer.material instantiates a per-renderer material copy. Unity's documentation says the caller must destroy these copies, and only Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets or a scene load frees them otherwise. A RunBot hero has Body, Nose, Fin_L and Fin_R renderers (the health bar is excluded), so each spawn creates 4 instances. RunDirector destroys bots (lines 204, 257) but never the materials. There is no scene change during a session, so the instances accumulate across islands and runs (Horde respawns every 1.5 s). The memory per instance is small, so this will not freeze the game by itself, but it grows without bound. This overlaps with the perf dimension's renderer.material item.
findings.fix: Use a MaterialPropertyBlock for the flash and stun tint, as HandMenuButton.ApplyVisuals already does, and read the base color from sharedMaterial. Alternatively, keep the instances and Destroy them in HeroHealth.OnDestroy.
findings.vnote: Verified. HeroHealth.Awake:81 accesses r.material for each child renderer of RunBotHero. Per the prefab hierarchy those are Body, Nose, Fin_L and Fin_R under Visual. HealthBar is excluded because healthBarFill points at it, and the GroundMarker disc and the two LineRenderers are siblings of RunBotHero, not children. So 4 instances per spawn. RunDirector destroys bots (204, 257) but never these materials. Nothing calls Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets and there is no scene load, so they accumulate across islands and runs. Small memory growth, not a freeze by itself. Overlaps with the perf renderer.material item.

missed.title: After any frame hitch over 200 ms, the explicit-Euler spring damping flips every clutched hero's velocity, so heroes lurch backward right after a freeze
missed.code:
velocity += toTarget * (p.Stiffness * dt);
velocity -= velocity * (p.Damping * dt);
missed.frequency: per frame whose Time.deltaTime > 0.2 s (Damping 5; TimeManager 'Maximum Allowed Timestep: 0.33333334'), i.e. on every reported hitch/freeze; affects the player hero while clutched and every bot, since bots always hold the clutch
missed.detail: FlyingCharacter.Update (FlyingCharacter.cs:109-122) passes raw Time.deltaTime, which Unity caps at 0.333 s. With Damping = 5, the factor (1 - 5*dt) becomes negative for dt > 0.2. At dt = 0.333, v' = -0.67*(v + 3.33*toTarget). Example: a hero hovering 2 m from its target gets v' = -4.4 m/s and moves about 1.5 m away. A bot strafing at 10 m/s jumps about 4 m backward (up to maxSpeed*dt = 8.3 m). Following frames pull it back, so after each freeze the heroes visibly rubber-band, and the player's hero can be thrown into a beam. This is an aftermath of the hitch, not its cause, but it makes the reported freezes look worse. No EditMode test covers large dt (SpringFlightModelTests has none). Whether on-device hitches exceed 200 ms is not measured yet.
missed.fix: Make the step stable for any dt: use exponential decay (velocity *= Mathf.Exp(-p.Damping * dt); glide likewise with GlideDrag), and sub-step the spring in SpringFlightModel.Step (split dt into slices of at most 1/60 s), or clamp dt in FlyingCharacter.Update (Mathf.Min(Time.deltaTime, 1f/30f)). Add a Core test: a hero 2 m from its target stepped with dt = 0.333 must not end farther from the target.

missed.title: The clutch target is never clamped to the arena, so after pushing into a wall, floor or ceiling the hero (and the CURSOR marker) stays stuck until the hand undoes the hidden overshoot
missed.code:
_target += clutchDelta * positionScale;   // ClutchMapper, unclamped
// FlyingCharacter.cs:63  _target = GetArenaBounds().Clamp(worldPosition);  (only the hero's copy is clamped)
missed.frequency: per clutch drag that continues past an arena boundary. With positionScale 60, 5 cm of extra hand travel = 3 m of hidden overshoot, so this is common in a 35x20x35 m box
missed.detail: HandPuppeteerController.cs:72-76 calls character.SetTarget(clutch.Target). FlyingCharacter clamps its own _target, but ClutchMapper._target keeps accumulating outside the arena. When the player reverses the hand, the mapper target is still outside, the clamp keeps returning the same wall point, and the hero does not move until the hand travels back the full overshoot. The hero feels stuck to the wall (it is the hero that stops, not the headset). AimCursorModel.cs:24-25 has the same issue: Position is clamped but the inner mapper's _target is not, so the CURSOR marker sticks at walls too. AimCursorModelTests.Drag_ClampedToBounds only checks the clamped position, not reversing out of it. BotBrain is unaffected because its mirrored _clutchTarget steps toward an already-clamped desired point. It is possible this is intentional, but the mouse-style mapping intent (ClutchMapper header, ADR 6) implies no accumulation past the edge.
missed.fix: Clamp inside the mapper. Give ClutchMapper.Step an ArenaBounds parameter (or a clamp callback) and set _target = bounds.Clamp(_target + clutchDelta * positionScale). HandPuppeteerController passes character.Bounds, and AimCursorModel passes its bounds. Add EditMode tests: drag 1 m of hand past the +X wall, then step -0.01 m, and expect the target/marker to move 0.6 m back immediately.

dimensions.notes:
I edited nothing; all reads were read-only.

Logic hangs ruled out: Core/*.cs and RunDirector have no unbounded loop or blocking call. PortalRoller is capped at 64 attempts, ChestRoller and HeroStats loops are bounded, and RunDirector's spawn `while` loop is bounded by MaxAlive because SpawnBot always adds to _bots. A logic hang cannot explain the random freeze. Core allocates only on events (HeroStats.From per kill or chest, Inventory.Add's FindIndex lambda per pick, RunChoiceText.Layout per panel refresh). The per-frame allocations Core contributes come from HandProto calling its string formatters every frame (RF-3).

Two items bear directly on the freeze report. (1) BC-3: any hitch over 200 ms ends with heroes lurching backwards because the explicit-Euler damping flips sign, so the hitch looks worse than it is. (2) BC-5: a false wrist pause sets timeScale 0, which a player may call a 'freeze'. The device test should note whether the PAUSED banner or pause panel appeared. Auto-pause from OnApplicationFocus and the userPresence check also stops the game and shows PAUSED.

Requested edge cases that are unreachable with the current catalog, so not reported as findings:
- Scaling.Hyperbolic clamps the base to <= 0.99 but has no lower clamp. A negative base hits 1/0 at some level (base -1, level 2 gives -inf). Every catalog base is positive.
- Scaling.Exponential divides by k, and k = 0 gives NaN. StatEffect never passes k, so the default 1 always applies.
- Reroll price overflow: (int)Math.Ceiling(25*1.2*1.5^n) passes int.MaxValue at about n = 45 rerolls. That is unaffordable long before then, and a negative result is rejected by TrySpend(amount < 0).
- Negative prices are impossible.
- Revives: only Second Wind gives one; it is unique, _revivesUsed resets at StartRun, and RunStateMachineTests covers revive once then Defeat.
- Island indexing is consistent. Enemy scaling uses island - 1. The shop uses islandIndex = Island (4), the 0-based index of island 5, and Economy tests cover it.
- Max-level items: stack items have MaxLevel 0 (uncapped), so the theme and Random pools can never empty. That is the only thing keeping BC-6 latent.

Test gaps that hide the bugs above:
- No ReportPlayerDeath-while-paused test (BC-1).
- No test that the RunStateMachine choice methods are gated while paused (RF-4).
- No reverse-drag-after-clamp test for AimCursorModel or ClutchMapper (BC-4).
- No fist-after-visible test for WristMenuGesture (BC-5).
- No large-dt SpringFlightModel test (BC-3).
- No 'never zero portals' test (BC-6).
- No validation tests for RunParams, TriggerGesture settle 0, or the tutorial telegraph time 0 (BC-7/8/9).
- Nothing checks that two simultaneously spawned bots get different seeds (BC-2).

Outside this dimension, noted for the perf auditors:
- HandGestureTracker.FindSubsystem allocates a new List and builds report strings (string.Join plus interpolation) every frame whenever no hand subsystem is running.
- HeroHealth.SetVisible calls GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true) on every death and respawn.
- HeroHealth and HandPuppeteerController use r.material, unlike HandMenuButton, which uses a MaterialPropertyBlock.

Rough effort for this dimension, as agent time plus a compile/EditMode run, excluding device testing:
- BC-1 to BC-5 with tests: about 3-4 h.
- BC-6 to BC-9: about 1 h.
- RF-1 (bot pooling) together with RF-2 (beam FX pool): about 4-6 h, including scene-builder changes and a rebuild.
- RF-3 (HUD change keys): about 1-2 h.
- RF-4, RF-5 and RF-6: about 3-4 h.
- RF-7: about 1-2 h.
Total is roughly 13-19 h, about 1.5-2 working days, followed by one Quest device pass.

findings.title: In RUN, a death RunDirector ignores falls back to the Quick Match auto-respawn: free full heal, and the hero comes back on the DEFEAT screen
findings.code:
if (_run.Phase != RunPhase.Island) return;
if (_run.ReportPlayerDeath()) playerHealth.Revive(_run.ReviveHealth(playerHealth.MaxHealth));
findings.frequency: per-player-death (Defeat path: every defeat; ignored-death path: rare race on a pause or island-clear frame)
findings.detail: HeroHealthModel.Tick (HeroHealthModel.cs:138-144) always respawns a dead hero at full health after RespawnDelay, and HeroHealth.Update:172 calls Respawn() when it does. RUN mode never turns this off. (1) Defeat: RunDirector's Victory/Defeat handler (RunDirector.cs:237-241) leaves the dead hero alone, so 3 s later it reappears at the spawn point with a full health bar under the DEFEAT banner, and Respawned fires (PointingBeamController.ResetAim). (2) Ignored deaths: RunStateMachine.ReportPlayerDeath returns false without Defeat while IsPaused (RunStateMachine.cs:217), and RunDirector returns early outside Island. Two ways to reach this: (a) MatchDirector or WristMenu pauses in Update, RunDirector.SyncPause mirrors it, and a run bot's PointingBeamController (order 0, input already sampled at -50) fires later in the same frame. (b) A Horde island clears inside RunDirector.Update: DespawnBots (RunDirector.cs:226) empties _bots before ApplyControls (RunDirector.cs:166), so the bots waiting for end-of-frame Destroy keep their input enabled and can still fire this frame. In both cases the death causes neither Defeat nor a revive, and the hero respawns at 100% HP. No test covers ReportPlayerDeath while paused (RunStateMachineTests only covers ReportBotKilled while paused).
findings.fix: Add an AutoRespawn flag to HealthParams/HeroHealth that RunDirector turns off during a run. Make ReportPlayerDeath accept the death even while paused (a lethal hit is a fact, not an input), or have RunDirector check Phase/IsDead after the pause resolves. In OnRunPhaseChanged, call SetControlled(false) on bots before Destroy. Add tests: death while paused leads to Defeat/revive; HeroHealthModel with auto-respawn off stays dead.
findings.vnote: The Defeat path is real. HeroHealthModel.Tick (HeroHealthModel.cs:138-144) resets a dead hero, and HeroHealth.Update:172 calls Respawn(). HeroHealth is not in fightOnly (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:233-234 wires only the input sources there), so it keeps ticking after the Defeat case in RunDirector.cs:237-241. About 3 s later the player hero reappears at its spawn point with a full health bar under the DEFEAT banner. The effect is cosmetic: input stays off. Race (a), a pause in the same frame, is REFUTED. When SyncPause pauses the run, ApplyControls in the same Update disables every bot input, and HandInputSourceBehaviour.OnDisable sets Current = default, so a later bot PointingBeamController reads no fire. A bot that fires earlier in the frame still sees _run.IsPaused false, so the death becomes Defeat or a revive. On paused frames dt is 0 and Time.time is frozen, so no new shot and no buffered shot can fire. Race (b), the Horde clear, is real: DespawnBots at line 226 runs inside Tick before ApplyControls at line 166, so the despawned bots stay enabled for that frame. It needs a bot's one-frame fire edge on the exact frame the 45 s timer expires, a bot controller that runs after RunDirector, and a lethal hit, so it is very rare. Arena clears are safe because a dead bot cannot fire (BotInputSource.Sample and PointingBeamController lines 204/223 check IsAlive). No test covers ReportPlayerDeath while paused (confirmed). Not a freeze cause.

findings.title: Bots spawned in the same frame share an RNG seed (Environment.TickCount), so they fire in sync with the same jitter and aim error
findings.code: _brain = new BotBrain(CurrentParams(), seed != 0 ? seed : System.Environment.TickCount);
findings.frequency: per-spawn (every island start with MaxAlive 2: Arena islands 3+ and Horde)
findings.detail: The RunBot prefab's BotInputSource keeps seed = 0 (HandHeroSceneBuilder.BotControllers never sets it, lines 666-667). RunDirector spawns up to MaxAlive bots in one frame with `while (_run.WantsSpawn(_bots.Count) && SpawnBot()) { }` (RunDirector.cs:178), so each Awake reads the same millisecond TickCount. BotBrain then draws identical sequences: the initial strafe timer (Reset -> NextStrafeSwitch), the fire jitter, the evade side and the AimError components. Both bots start _fireTimer = FireInterval with the same jitter, so they telegraph and fire on the same frame until one of them is hit and evades. The result is double-damage volleys that are much harder to dodge than intended, and RunDirector.seed cannot reproduce bot behaviour. The test BotBrainTests.SameSeed_SameMatch shows that identical seeds give identical matches.
findings.fix: Have RunDirector own a System.Random built from its seed and pass `rng.Next()` into RunBot.Setup, then into a BotInputSource.Reseed(int) that recreates or reseeds the BotBrain. The Quick Match bot keeps its own seed.
findings.vnote: Seed 0 on the RunBot prefab is confirmed: BotControllers SetRefs(botInput, ...) at HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:666-667 never sets seed. Both bots are spawned in one while loop (RunDirector.cs:178), and Awake runs inside Instantiate even though the prefab's input is disabled. Environment.TickCount has millisecond resolution, so equal seeds are likely, but that is not verified: two Instantiates of this prefab, each cloning 4 materials in HeroHealth.Awake, may cross a millisecond boundary. Equal seeds also desync quickly. The wall-pin FlipStrafe (BotBrain.cs:256) depends on position, and the bots spawn at different points. Correction: the claim that both bots start with the same jitter is wrong. Reset sets _fireTimer = _p.FireInterval with NO jitter (BotBrain.cs:136), and Reset runs on every BotInputSource.OnEnable. The first volley is therefore synchronized whatever the seeds are, and every pause/resume re-synchronizes all bots. The proposed reseed fix alone will not stop synced volleys (see missed BC-M1).

findings.title: SpringFlightModel's explicit damping turns velocity backwards on frames longer than 0.2 s: after a hitch the hero lurches up to ~8 m away from the hand target
findings.code:
velocity += toTarget * (p.Stiffness * dt);
velocity -= velocity * (p.Damping * dt);
findings.frequency: per-frame for every hero (FlyingCharacter.Update); misbehaves only on frames with dt > 1/Damping = 0.2 s
findings.detail: With FlyingCharacter defaults (stiffness 10, damping 5), a frame with dt = 0.333 s (Time.deltaTime is capped near 1/3 s, the default maximumDeltaTime) gives v = (v0 + 3.33*toTarget) * (1 - 1.67) = -0.67*(...). Velocity points away from the target. ClampMagnitude caps it at maxSpeed 25 m/s, and the position moves 25*0.333 = 8.3 m the wrong way in one step. Every freeze over 200 ms (the reported symptom) therefore ends with the player hero and every bot visibly jumping backwards, which makes the hitch look worse. SpringFlightModelTests uses only small dt.
findings.fix: Use frame-rate-independent damping, `velocity *= Mathf.Exp(-p.Damping * dt)` (same for GlideDrag), and/or sub-step when dt > 1/60 (for example, a loop of fixed 1/90 s steps capped at 4). Add a test: one step of dt = 0.33 with the clutch held never moves the hero away from the target.
findings.vnote: The code is at SpringFlightModel.cs:90-91. ProjectSettings/TimeManager.asset has Maximum Allowed Timestep 0.33333334, so after a stall dt reaches 0.333 and the damping factor is 1 - 5*0.333 = -0.667. Velocity flips away from the target, ClampMagnitude caps it at 25 m/s, and the position moves up to 8.3 m the wrong way. The flipped velocity then decays over about 0.2 s (damping 5/s), so the hero keeps drifting away before the spring pulls it back. Bots always hold the clutch (BotBrain.Step sets ClutchHeld = true), so every bot does this on any frame over 200 ms. The glide branch is safe because 0.8 * 0.333 < 1. This does not cause the freeze. It makes every freeze over 200 ms end in a visible lurch of heroes and bots. Fix and test are as proposed.

findings.title: ClutchMapper's target is never clamped, so dragging past a wall creates a dead zone the hand must undo (puppeteer and CURSOR marker)
findings.code: _target += clutchDelta * positionScale;
findings.frequency: per-frame while a clutch or aim grip is held near an arena wall
findings.detail: FlyingCharacter.SetTarget (FlyingCharacter.cs:63) clamps only its copy of the target, and AimCursorModel (AimCursorModel.cs:24-25) clamps only Position. The mapper's internal _target keeps accumulating outside the 35x20x35 box. With positionScale 60, overshooting a wall by 5 cm of hand travel puts the target 3 m outside, and the hero or cursor stays pinned until the hand moves 5 cm back. AimCursorModelTests.Drag_ClampedToBounds drags 1 m (target 60 m out, 42.5 m past the wall) but never drags back, which hides this. The bot is unaffected because BotBrain mirrors and clamps its own target.
findings.fix: Give ClutchMapper.Step an ArenaBounds (or a Clamp callback) and clamp _target in place: `_target = bounds.Clamp(_target + delta*scale)`. HandPuppeteerController passes character.Bounds and AimCursorModel passes its bounds. Add a test: drag past the wall, reverse 1 cm, and the position moves 0.6 m inward at once.
findings.vnote: ClutchMapper.cs:49 accumulates _target with no clamp. FlyingCharacter.SetTarget (line 63) clamps only its own copy, and AimCursorModel.Step (line 25) clamps only Position. The mapper's internal target keeps drifting outside the box, which leaves a dead zone of overshoot * 60 that the hand must undo. The test gap is confirmed: AimCursorModelTests.Drag_ClampedToBounds (lines 73-78) drags 1 m and never back. Releasing and regrabbing recovers, because a grab restarts from the clamped position. The effect is on control feel, which players see; it is not a freeze.

findings.title: Once the wrist button is visible, the fist rule no longer applies: closing the left hand into a clutch can toggle pause
findings.frequency: per-frame (WristMenu.Update, unscaled time) during every match/run phase
findings.detail: MaxFistStrength only gates showing the button. After IsVisible is true, Step returns `wasVisible && IsVisible && pinched` with no fist check (line 73). The left hand is the clutch hand. PinchTrigger's own header comment says a closed fist reads as a pinch, so an open left palm that faces the head for 0.25 s and then closes to grab produces a pinch rising edge, and WristMenu.cs:58 calls director.TogglePause(). That sets Time.timeScale = 0 and the whole game stops. The PAUSED banner should appear, so check during the device test whether some reported 'freezes' were unintended pauses. WristMenuGestureTests has no test for a fist closing after the button is visible.
findings.fix: Hide the button (or ignore the press) while fistStrength > MaxFistStrength even when visible, and/or require the pinch with fist strength below the limit: `return wasVisible && IsVisible && pinched && fistStrength <= p.MaxFistStrength;`. Add a test that closing a fist after Shown() never presses.
findings.vnote: The code at WristMenuGesture.cs:67-73 matches the finding: MaxFistStrength gates only showing the button, and the press at line 73 has no fist check. On the device, a fist closing must take the thumb-tip/index-tip pinch value (HandGestureTracker around lines 217-223) from below 0.5 to above 0.8 while the palm still faces the head (hide threshold 0.4). PinchTrigger's own comment says a fist reads as a pinch, so this is believable but unmeasured. An accidental pause shows the PAUSED banner (MatchHud.cs:43), the wrist label flips to RESUME, and hands and head tracking keep working. It is therefore unlikely to be what Hyun calls a headset freeze, but it is worth one device check.

findings.title: PortalRoller can return zero portals and ChoosePortal has no fallback: a phase with no buttons and no exit except MENU (latent)
findings.code:
_portals = PortalRoller.Roll(next, Inventory, _rng);
Enter(RunPhase.ChoosePortal);
findings.frequency: per-island-transition (8 times per run)
findings.detail: PortalRoller.Roll (PortalRoller.cs:72-82) skips every combination whose chest pool is empty and gives up after 64 attempts, so an empty list is a legal result. OpenChest guards against an empty chest (RunStateMachine.cs:335-339), but OfferPortals enters ChoosePortal regardless, and RunChoiceMenu then shows a header with zero buttons. Today this cannot happen only because every stack item has MaxLevel 0 (uncapped, ItemCatalog Stack(... false, 0 ...)), so the Damage/Health/Random pools are never empty. Capping item levels in a later balance pass would make the softlock reachable. PortalRollerTests checks 'never an empty chest' but not 'never zero portals'.
findings.fix: In OfferPortals, if the roll is empty, fall back to a guaranteed portal (for example Arena + Random, or Arena + Upgrade) or go straight to BeginIsland(next, fallback). Add a test with a fully maxed inventory.
findings.vnote: OfferPortals (RunStateMachine.cs:362-363) enters ChoosePortal with no empty check, and PortalRoller.Roll can legally return an empty list after 64 attempts. Today this is unreachable. Every Stack item has MaxLevel 0, and Inventory.CanAdd (Inventory.cs:47) treats that as uncapped. So the Damage pool (PowerCell/RapidCoil/FocusLens), the Random pool and the Epic pool (Deflector) are never empty. Latent only.

findings.title: RunParams.MaxAlive <= 0 means Arena islands never spawn a bot and never clear (softlock from an inspector value)
findings.code: spec.MaxAlive = Mathf.Min(spec.BotCount, p.MaxAlive);
findings.frequency: per-island start; RunDirector re-applies the inspector `rules` every frame (RunDirector.cs:114)
findings.detail: WantsSpawn returns false when `alive >= Spec.MaxAlive` (line 209). With MaxAlive 0, Arena never spawns, so _islandKills never reaches BotCount and the Island phase never exits. Horde islands silently become empty 45 s timers. Elite and Boss keep a hard-coded MaxAlive of 1. RunParams has no validation, and the field is live-tunable in the inspector.
findings.fix: Clamp in RunRules.Island: `Mathf.Max(1, p.MaxAlive)`, or add RunParams.Validate()/OnValidate in RunDirector. Add a test for MaxAlive 0.
findings.vnote: With MaxAlive <= 0, WantsSpawn (line 209) never spawns, so an Arena island never clears and a Horde island becomes an empty 45 s timer. Elite and Boss keep MaxAlive 1 from the defaults at lines 83-84.
