Note that Spec is computed in BeginIsland, so a live inspector change takes effect only at the next island, even though Params is re-assigned every frame. This needs an inspector value; latent.

findings.title: TriggerGesture with gripSettleTime <= 0: a pull without the gun grip never fires and only charges
findings.code:
_pending = gripSettleTime; // wait: the grip may still be closing
return default;
findings.frequency: per-frame (XRHandsInputSource.Sample) on each index pull in CURSOR mode
findings.detail: With gripSettleTime = 0, _pending becomes 0. On the next step `_pending > 0f` is false, so the method falls through to `Fired = false, Held = _index.IsOn`. The pull never fires a normal shot, but Held=true starts a charge (PointingBeamController maps TriggerHeld to PinchHeld). The inspector value defaults to 0.15 (XRHandsInputSource.cs:40), so this is latent, but the field is exposed for tuning and no test covers 0.
findings.fix: Treat gripSettleTime <= 0 as 'fire immediately': `if (gripSettleTime <= 0f) return new TriggerState { Fired = true, Held = true };`, or use a separate bool _pendingActive instead of _pending > 0. Add a test for settle 0.
findings.vnote: Traced: with gripSettleTime 0, the rising edge sets _pending = 0 and returns default. On the next step `_pending > 0f` is false, so the method returns Fired false and Held true. No normal shot fires; the pull only charges. The default is 0.15 (XRHandsInputSource.cs:40) and the scene builder does not override it. Latent.

findings.title: TutorialSequencer.TelegraphProgress divides by DodgeTelegraphTime with no guard (NaN line width at 0)
findings.code: public float TelegraphProgress => IsTelegraphing ? Mathf.Clamp01(_dodgeTimer / Params.DodgeTelegraphTime) : 0f;
findings.frequency: per-frame during the tutorial Dodge step (TutorialDirector.UpdateTelegraph)
findings.detail: With DodgeTelegraphTime = 0 (an inspector field on TutorialDirector.steps), the first telegraph frame computes 0/0 = NaN. Mathf.Clamp01 returns NaN unchanged, and TutorialDirector feeds it into LineRenderer.widthMultiplier and Color.Lerp. BotBrain.TelegraphProgress already guards this case (`_p.TelegraphTime > 0f`). The two disagree.
findings.fix: Guard it like BotBrain: `Params.DodgeTelegraphTime > 0f ? Mathf.Clamp01(...) : 1f`.
findings.vnote: TickDodge (TutorialSequencer.cs:142-145) sets IsTelegraphing and _dodgeTimer = 0, then returns. With DodgeTelegraphTime 0, TutorialDirector.UpdateTelegraph (line 195) reads 0/0 = NaN for exactly one frame. Mathf.Clamp01 returns NaN unchanged (all its comparisons are false), and the NaN goes into widthMultiplier and Color.Lerp. The next tick fires. This needs an inspector value of 0 and lasts one frame; latent nit.

findings.title: RunBot lifecycle has to become reset-able before bots can be pooled (Instantiate/Destroy, closure subscription, per-spawn material instances, Awake-time seed)
findings.frequency: per-spawn / per-kill (Horde islands: every 1.5 s respawn), Destroy at RunDirector.cs:204 and 257
findings.detail: To pool bots: (1) the Died lambda is added per spawn and never removed, so reusing an instance would double-count kills. (2) HeroHealth.Awake (HeroHealth.cs:77-82) calls r.material on every renderer, creating 4 material instances per bot that Destroy does not free (they leak until UnloadUnusedAssets). Pooling makes Awake run once. (3) BotInputSource builds its BotBrain and seed in Awake (cause of BC-2). (4) PointingBeamController initialises aim in Start, and its beam, charge and cooldown state carries over. All reset hooks already exist: HeroHealth.ResetHealth/SetHealthScale, BotBrain.Reset, FlyingCharacter.Respawn, PointingBeamController.ResetAim, ImpactFlash.OnEnable. They only need to be gathered in one place.
findings.fix: Add RunBot.Activate(Vector3 at, IslandSpec spec, int seed) and RunBot.Deactivate(). Activate does SetActive(true), Setup, reseeds the brain, resets aim, beam and charge. Deactivate does SetActive(false), cancels the charge and hides the beam/telegraph. Add `public event Action<RunBot> Died` on RunBot, subscribed once inside RunBot. RunDirector keeps a Stack<RunBot> pool and pre-warms MaxAlive(=2)+1 instances at BeginRun. Replace r.material in HeroHealth with MaterialPropertyBlock (the HandMenuButton pattern). This fixes BC-2 and the material leak along the way.
findings.vnote: The code is at RunDirector.cs:192-195 and 204/257. The lambda is never unsubscribed, which only matters once bots are pooled. HeroHealth.Awake (line 81) calls r.material on every non-bar renderer. The bot hero has Body, Nose, Fin_L and Fin_R (builder lines 480-492), so each spawn creates 4 material instances. Destroy does not free them (the Renderer.material contract), and nothing here calls UnloadUnusedAssets, so a run leaks a few hundred small materials. BotInputSource builds its brain in Awake, and PointingBeamController calls ResetAim in Start: both confirmed. Horde respawns come 1.5 s after each kill. Re-rated from high to medium. Instantiating this small prefab plus 4 material clones costs milliseconds, which can drop a frame but cannot explain a multi-hundred-ms freeze. Pooling is still the right refactor. A pooled bot must also reset the HeroHealthModel respawn timer and get a jittered BotBrain.Reset (BC-M1).

findings.title: PointingBeamController (426 lines) mixes aim, charge/cooldown, hit resolution, beam visuals, impact FX and audio; split out a pooled BeamFx
findings.code:
GameObject fx = Instantiate(hitEffectPrefab, end, Quaternion.LookRotation(-dir));
Destroy(fx, 1f);
findings.frequency: per-hit (Instantiate + Destroy); CollectCandidates per-frame per shooter
findings.detail: Fire() (lines 346-395) does the damage raycast, two GetComponentInParent calls, BeamHitReceiver dispatch, FX Instantiate/Destroy, LineRenderer styling and audio. The player and every bot run this same class. ImpactFlash already deactivates itself after 0.25 s (ImpactFlash.cs:22-25) while the beam destroys it after 1 s, so a SetActive pool drops straight in once FX spawning sits behind one method. Related smells that cause bugs: `_aimPoint != Vector3.zero` (line 212) and `_rawAimPoint == Vector3.zero` (line 270) use the zero vector as 'no aim yet', yet the normal-shot path (line 224) has no such check, so the two paths disagree. `foreach (AimAssistTarget t in AimAssistTarget.All)` (line 324) enumerates an IReadOnlyList, which boxes the enumerator on every frame for every shooter.
findings.fix: Extract a BeamFx component (LineRenderer + timer + color/width + PlayOneShot) and a static ImpactFxPool (Get/Return via SetActive; ImpactFlash returns itself instead of SetActive(false) + Destroy). Keep aim selection (UpdateAim/UpdateCursor/CollectCandidates) in an AimSelector class. Replace the zero sentinel with a bool _hasAimPoint. Expose AimAssistTarget.All as List<T> or iterate with a for loop over Count.
findings.vnote: PointingBeamController.cs:370-373 calls Instantiate plus Destroy(fx, 1f) on every hit, and ImpactFlash already deactivates itself at 0.25 s (lines 22-25), so a SetActive pool drops in easily. The foreach at line 324 goes through IReadOnlyList (AimAssistTarget.All returns the backing List as IReadOnlyList, line 13), which boxes the enumerator: about 1 small allocation per shooter per frame. CollectCandidates also runs every frame for bots in UpdateAim even though the builder sets the bot's assistAngle to 0, so that work is wasted on the bot path. The zero sentinel is inconsistent but harmless here: ArenaCenter is (0,2,20), so the reset cursor is never exactly the zero vector. Each effect is small, so this is low for both freezes and player-visible bugs; it is a worthwhile cleanup.

findings.title: The HUD rebuilds every string every LateUpdate; RunHudText is pure, so a change key makes 'update only when the value changes' trivial
findings.code:
if (inMatch) scoreLine.text = ScoreText(m);
else if (inRun) scoreLine.text = RunStatusText(r);
findings.frequency: per-frame (LateUpdate), for both scoreLine and banner
findings.detail: RunStatusText calls RunHudText.Objective, then Status, then IslandName. That is enum ToString() + ToUpperInvariant() + 2-3 interpolated strings + concatenation every frame, plus BannerText/RunBannerText ($"ROUND {m.Round}\n..." and IntroBanner). The displayed values change at most a few times per second: island, type, botsLeft, crystals, RoundToInt(hp), RoundToInt(max), CeilToInt(seconds), phase, paused. RunChoiceMenu.ShopKey (RunChoiceMenu.cs:193) already uses this change-key idea, but its `foreach (ShopSlot slot in shop.Slots)` over an IReadOnlyList boxes an enumerator every frame while the shop is open.
findings.fix: In MatchHud, build a small readonly struct HudKey (ints and enums) per frame, compare it with the last one, and only then call RunHudText and assign .text. In RunHudText, replace IslandName's ToString().ToUpperInvariant() with a static string[] indexed by (int)type, and likewise RunChoiceText.ChestName and Rarity. In ShopKey, iterate with `for (int i = 0; i < slots.Count; i++)`.
findings.vnote: MatchHud.LateUpdate (lines 37-38, 43-45) rebuilds RunStatusText every frame. That is enum ToString plus ToUpperInvariant, three string.Format calls with boxed ints, and concatenation: roughly 12-15 allocations, about 1 KB per frame on an island, or about 70-90 KB/s. However, the TMP setter in this project (com.unity.ugui TMP_Text.cs:128) returns early when the new string equals the old one, so the mesh is NOT rebuilt every frame; the cost is GC garbage only. With incremental GC on, this is the largest steady per-frame allocator found, but it is unlikely to cause a stall of hundreds of ms by itself. Re-rated from high to medium. ShopKey's foreach over IReadOnlyList<ShopSlot> (Economy.cs:121, RunChoiceMenu.cs:193) is confirmed but runs only while the shop is open.

findings.title: Two pause states (MatchStateMachine and RunStateMachine) are synced by per-frame polling, and the choice methods gate on pause inconsistently
findings.frequency: per-frame (RunDirector.Update); the mismatch window lasts one frame per pause or resume
findings.detail: RunStateMachine has its own IsPaused, Pause, Resume and a PausedChanged event that nothing subscribes to. RunDirector copies the match pause once per Update. The gates are mixed: PickChestItem, ChoosePortal and LeaveShop check `!Paused` (the match) in RunDirector.cs:88-92, while BuyShopItem and RerollShop rely on `_run.IsPaused` inside RunStateMachine (lines 246/251), and RunStateMachine.PickChestItem/ChoosePortal/LeaveShop (235-269) ignore IsPaused entirely. Because of the polling, the run is 'unpaused' for part of the frame in which the match pauses, which opens the BC-1 race. After Victory/Defeat a match pause makes SyncPause call _run.Pause() (which returns false) on every frame.
findings.fix: Subscribe RunDirector to MatchStateMachine.PausedChanged and pause or resume the run synchronously, or remove pause from RunStateMachine and pass `paused` into Tick and the Report* methods. Gate every choice method in RunStateMachine the same way and add tests for each one while paused.
findings.vnote: Nothing subscribes to RunStateMachine.PausedChanged (grep: only MatchStateMachine.PausedChanged has a subscriber). The gating is inconsistent as described: RunDirector.cs:88-92 checks the match's pause in some choice methods and the run's pause in others, and RunStateMachine lines 235-269 has the same split. After Victory or Defeat, a match pause makes SyncPause call _run.Pause() every frame, which returns false; harmless. The claim that this opens the BC-1 race is wrong for the pause case (see BC-1). The choice panels hide once the run is paused, so the one-frame window has little player impact.

findings.title: Control gating and death handling are spread across three paths (MatchDirector.fightOnly/opponentOnly, RunDirector.ApplyControls per bot, HeroHealthModel auto-respawn)
findings.frequency: per-event (MatchDirector) plus per-frame (RunDirector.ApplyControls loops every bot, RunDirector.cs:162-168)
findings.detail: The Quick Match bot is gated through the opponentOnly Behaviour[], run bots through RunBot.SetControlled from RunDirector every frame, and the player through fightOnly plus SetRunControls. Both directors subscribe to playerHealth.Died (MatchDirector.cs:79, RunDirector.cs:60), and both reset hero health on their own phase changes. Neither says who owns respawn, which is how BC-1 arises. Because despawn happens before the gating update (DespawnBots inside Tick, then ApplyControls), dying bots stay live for the rest of the frame.
findings.fix: Add one ControlGate(bool playerLive, bool enemiesLive) that is applied on events (phase change, pause change, run phase change, bot spawn) instead of per frame. RunBot.Deactivate (RF-1) disables input before despawn. Make the death policy explicit: HeroHealth.AutoRespawn is true in Quick Match and false in a run, where RunDirector decides between revive and Defeat.
findings.vnote: Verified MatchDirector.cs:235-242, the per-frame loop in RunDirector.ApplyControls (lines 162-168), both Died subscriptions (MatchDirector.cs:79, RunDirector.cs:60), and despawn before gating within one Update. As an ownership and design observation it is accurate and explains race (b) in BC-1. Its direct runtime impact is small.

findings.title: Hero stats are computed in two places with different caching (RunStateMachine.Stats uncached, RunHeroStats cached)
findings.code: public HeroStats Stats => HeroStats.From(Inventory);
findings.frequency: per-kill, per-clear, per-death, per-chest roll (ChestRoller.cs:40 recomputes again)
findings.detail: Each access to RunStateMachine.Stats or RevivesLeft re-folds the whole inventory. HeroStats.From iterates IReadOnlyList interfaces, so it boxes 1 + 2*N enumerators per call. RunHeroStats (RunHeroStats.cs:18-30) caches the same fold by Inventory.TotalLevels. The two caches can disagree if anything ever mutates an inventory outside Add (not possible today), and future stat users will not know which one to call.
findings.fix: Move the cache into Inventory (`public HeroStats Stats` recomputed when TotalLevels changes), or into RunStateMachine. RunHeroStats and ChestRoller then read inventory.Stats. Inside HeroStats.From, use for-loops over Count.
findings.vnote: RunStateMachine.Stats (line 149) recomputes HeroStats.From on every access. Callers are per-kill (ReportBotKilled to KillReward), per-clear, per-death (RevivesLeft), HealAfterClear and ChestRoller.Roll (line 40), so none of them is per frame. HeroStats.From uses foreach over Inventory.Items and over Effects/Debuffs, all exposed as IReadOnlyList (ItemDefinition.cs:71-72), so it boxes 1+2N enumerators per call. This is low-frequency garbage and a duplicated-cache smell. Not a freeze cause.

findings.title: The scene builder wires fields by string and only logs on a missing field; BuildScene is a 320-line method. The perf refactors will rename fields
findings.frequency: once per scene build (batch -executeMethod)
findings.detail: SetRefs and SetArray (lines 780-809) look up serialized fields by name and `continue` past a missing one. A batch build still saves Arena_Main.unity and BuildScript makes an APK whose references are null. RF-1 and RF-2 move fields such as beam and hitEffectPrefab into new components, so a typo would ship silently broken bots. BuildScene (lines 82-405) builds the player, bot, run director, HUD, menus, wrist menu and tutorial inline, which makes adding pool roots or pre-warm counts error-prone.
findings.fix: Collect missing fields and throw at the end of BuildScene (or call EditorApplication.Exit(1) in batch mode) so the build fails loudly. Split BuildScene into BuildPlayer, BuildQuickMatchBot, BuildRun, BuildHudAndMenus and BuildTutorial helpers that return the components they create. Optionally use nameof() for field names through [SerializeField] internal accessors.
findings.vnote: SetRefs and SetArray (HandHeroSceneBuilder.cs:780-809) call LogError and continue, and BuildScene (82-405) still saves the scene. BuildScript.BuildQuestApk calls BuildAll and fails only on an OpenXR validation error or a BuildPlayer error. AUTO/tools/compile_check.ps1 greps the log only for 'error CS'. A field renamed by the perf refactor would therefore ship an APK with null references. Some direct FindProperty(...).floatValue/colorValue calls (for example beamColor and ringRadius) would throw instead, so the behaviour is mixed. This is a build-safety risk for the planned refactor, not a runtime freeze.

missed.title: BotBrain.Reset starts every bot's fire timer at exactly FireInterval (no jitter), so bots spawned together, and all bots after every resume, telegraph and fire on the same frame regardless of seed
missed.frequency: per-spawn (RunDirector spawns MaxAlive=2 in one frame on Arena 3+ and Horde) and per-resume (RunBot.SetControlled(true) re-enables BotInputSource, and its OnEnable at BotInputSource.cs:50 calls _brain.Reset())
missed.detail: Both bots use the same BotDifficulty and the same _fireIntervalScale. After Reset, UpdateShooting decrements _fireTimer by the same dt from the first Step (Perceive sets _hasPerceived on that first step). Both therefore reach 0 on the same frame, as long as both are within MaxFireRange 40 m, which almost always holds in the 35 m arena. Both telegraph for TelegraphTime and fire on the same frame. Jitter is applied only after a shot (lines 276/287). Every pause/resume runs SetControlled(false) and then SetControlled(true), so OnDisable/OnEnable call Reset and re-synchronize all bots again. This is the deterministic cause of the double volleys that BC-2 attributes to equal seeds. The BC-2 fix (distinct seeds) does not change it.
missed.fix: Randomize the first interval in Reset, for example `_fireTimer = _p.FireInterval + (float)_rng.NextDouble() * _p.FireIntervalJitter;` or a fraction like `_p.FireInterval * (0.6f + 0.4f * (float)_rng.NextDouble())`. Combine it with BC-2's per-bot seeds from RunDirector's RNG. Check the BotBrainTests that assume first-shot timing (several set FireIntervalJitter = 0, lines 61 and 202, and those keep passing). Add a test: two brains with different seeds and default jitter do not fire their first shot on the same step.

findings.title: When the aim hand loses tracking, the reticle and hero freeze with no feedback. This may be the reported "freeze", and nobody separated it from a render stall
findings.code:
if (!aimHand.IsTracked)
    return data; // HasAim = false: reticle freezes at the last aim point
findings.frequency: per-frame while the aim hand is untracked (hand leaves the camera FOV, one hand occludes the other while clutching, fast motion, poor light)
findings.detail: None of the six auditors asked which kind of freeze Hyun sees. There are two kinds. (a) Image freeze: the world, the bots and the HUD stop while head rotation still reprojects. That is a main- or render-thread stall, which is what all the GC/spawn findings target. (b) Control freeze: the world keeps moving but your reticle and hero stop. The code produces (b) by design on every tracking dropout. HandGestureTracker.cs:146-151 keeps the last pose and sets IsTracked=false. XRHandsInputSource returns HasAim=false, so the reticle freezes at the last aim point. PointingBeamController.Update (line 189) then skips UpdateAim, ShotCooldown drops buffered shots (line 223), and the clutch opens, so the hero glides to a stop. A grep found no visual cue for hand-tracking loss anywhere in HandProto: IsTracked is read only by input code, HandMenuPointer and WristMenu. The game clutches with a left fist and aims with the right hand. Two-hand occlusion and hands drifting out of the Quest 3 tracking cameras are common, which fits 'random, not tied to an island'. The planned PerfSpikeLogger only fires on frame time over 50 ms, so it records nothing during episodes of type (b).
findings.fix: Ask Hyun one triage question in the device checklist: when it freezes, do the bots and the HUD keep moving? In PerfSpikeLogger, log transitions of HandGestureTracker.Instance.Left/Right.IsTracked (edge-triggered, with a timestamp) alongside the frame spikes. Add a cheap tracking-lost cue, for example tint or blink the reticle or ground marker while HasAim is false, so a tracking dropout is never mistaken for a hang.

findings.title: The PerfSpikeLogger spec as written would under-measure or miss the freezes it is meant to catch
findings.code: Maximum Allowed Timestep: 0.33333334
findings.frequency: per-frame (logger sampling); per-spike (file write)
findings.detail: (1) Time.deltaTime is capped at maximumDeltaTime (0.333 s here), and it is 0 while paused, because MatchDirector.cs:231 sets Time.timeScale = 0. A deltaTime-based detector would log a 2-second freeze as 333 ms and would see nothing in the pause or choice menus. (2) Writing to persistentDataPath from the main thread at the moment of a spike (File/StreamWriter, string formatting) adds its own hitch and allocates, which breaks the 'logger must not allocate' rule. (3) Step 2 of the request makes logs 'development build only'. If PerfSpikeLogger is put behind the same DEVELOPMENT_BUILD guard, the release APK, the one with representative timing, records nothing. (4) With incremental GC (gcIncremental 1 at ProjectSettings.asset:925), one collection cycle spans many frames. A GC.CollectionCount(0) delta in the spike frame neither proves nor rules out GC. I am not certain whether Time.unscaledDeltaTime is also capped, so the fix below avoids relying on it.
findings.fix: Measure the frame interval with Time.realtimeSinceStartupAsDouble (or Stopwatch.GetTimestamp) differences, which are neither clamped nor scaled. Keep a preallocated ring buffer of structs (time, frame ms, GC count, GC.GetTotalMemory(false), island, RunPhase, BotsAlive, timeScale, Application.isFocused, hand IsTracked flags). Format into a reused char[]/StringBuilder and flush only in OnApplicationPause(true), OnApplicationFocus(false), at menu return or every N seconds while out of combat. Compile the logger into both APKs (a serialized enable flag is fine), and gate only the chatty Debug.Log calls on DEVELOPMENT_BUILD.

findings.title: Device-level causes (head-tracking loss, system overlays, thermal throttling, compositor stale frames) are not observable, and nobody proposed the zero-code VrApi logcat capture
findings.code:
m_UpdateType: 0
  m_IgnoreTrackingState: 0
findings.frequency: per-event (OS tracking loss, overlay or throttle step)
findings.detail: The camera's TrackedPoseDriver honours the tracking state, so pose updates stop while the HMD is untracked. Quest's own tracking-lost handling and system overlays also look like 'the headset froze' to a player. MatchDirector pauses on focus loss and user-absence (lines 154-162, 204-213), and none of these transitions is logged anywhere. RS-9/RS-1 note that perf hints and frame-timing stats are off, so thermal clock drops and GPU-bound frames leave no trace either. The six audits are all static; nobody suggested the device telemetry Quest already emits. On Quest, the runtime prints a once-per-second performance line to logcat under the VrApi tag (FPS, stale frames, CPU/GPU levels, temperature, in Meta's documented logcat stats format). It distinguishes app stalls (FPS drop, Stale > 0) from throttling (CPU/GPU level changes) without any code change. I did not verify the exact field set on the current Horizon OS build.
findings.fix: Add to the PERF_REPORT adb section: `adb logcat -c` then `adb logcat -s VrApi:* Unity:* > freeze_session.txt` while playing, and note the wall-clock time of each freeze. Add to PerfSpikeLogger an edge-triggered record of the head InputDevice's isTracked/trackingState (reuse MatchDirector's _heads list; GetDevicesWithCharacteristics is allocation-free per GM-11's note), plus OnApplicationFocus and OnApplicationPause transitions with timestamps.

findings.title: BuildScript writes both APKs to the same dated path, so the second same-day build overwrites the first
findings.frequency: once per build
findings.detail: Step 4 of the request needs one Development Build APK and one normal APK. The output name contains only the date (line 58) and the options are hard-coded to BuildOptions.None (line 66). Adding a dev variant without changing the name makes the release build silently replace the dev APK, or the reverse, in ../Build. RS-2 noted the missing dev variant but not the name collision.
findings.fix: Add a BuildQuestApkDevelopment entry point (MenuItem plus executeMethod) that sets BuildOptions.Development (optionally AllowDebugging/ConnectWithProfiler) and builds HandHero_<yyyyMMdd_HHmm>_dev.apk; the release build gets a _release suffix. Log both paths in PERF_REPORT.

findings.title: Physics simulates at 100 Hz for nothing: no Rigidbody, no physics callbacks, queries only. A hitch is followed by up to 33 catch-up steps
findings.code:
m_SimulationMode: 0
  m_AutoSyncTransforms: 1
findings.frequency: per-physics-step (about 1.4 per frame at 72 Hz; up to 33 in the frame after a stall)
findings.detail: TimeManager.asset has Fixed Timestep m_Count 1411199 / m_Rate 141120000, which is 0.01 s (100 Hz, double the Unity default), and SimulationMode is FixedUpdate. The class-ID census of Arena_Main.unity, RunBot.prefab and BeamImpact.prefab has no Rigidbody (54), Animator or ParticleSystem, and a grep of HandProto and Core finds no OnTrigger, OnCollision, FixedUpdate or Rigidbody use. Physics is used only for RaycastNonAlloc, OverlapSphereNonAlloc and the menu-pointer raycast. Every simulation step is therefore pure overhead on top of the moving static colliders (SP-8). After any stall, Unity runs up to maximumDeltaTime / fixedDeltaTime = 33 steps in one frame, which lengthens the hitch it follows (RS-7 covers the time clamp, not the step count).
findings.fix: Set Physics.simulationMode = SimulationMode.Script in Project Settings and never call Simulate. Scene queries keep working because autoSyncTransforms (or an explicit Physics.SyncTransforms once per frame) updates the query structures. Alternatively, raise the fixed timestep back to 0.02. Device-check that beam hits, shockwave overlap and menu pointing still work.

findings.title: The test assembly references only HandHero.Core, so the pooling refactor of RunDirector, HeroHealth and PointingBeamController has no automated safety net
findings.code:
"references": [
        "HandHero.Core",
findings.frequency: n/a (process gap)
findings.detail: The 321 EditMode tests (tests.xml: 321/321 passed) can only reach Core. HandProto MonoBehaviours are outside any referenced assembly, and there is no PlayMode test assembly. The fixes ranked highest (SP-1/RF-1 bot pooling, SP-3 impact pooling, BR-4/BR-5 death handling, the HUD dirty-check) all live in HandProto. The pooled-bot reset checklist in the spawn auditor's notes (spawn position, Died subscription, beam state, seed) is exactly the regression class that only a device test would catch today. The request's step 4 ('tests pass') would pass trivially while those regressions ship.
findings.fix: Put the pool bookkeeping in Core as a pure class (for example BotPool<T> with Acquire/Release/ActiveCount, and the per-spawn reset contract as data) with EditMode tests: never exceeds MaxAlive+1, a released bot is reused, each acquire gets a fresh seed. Optionally add a minimal PlayMode asmdef that instantiates RunBot.prefab, kills it, releases and reacquires it, and asserts the reset state. Adding a PlayMode asmdef is new test infrastructure, so propose it to Hyun first.

findings.title: The Meta system gesture is not filtered: pinches during the OS gesture are read as game input, and the right-hand gesture opens the universal menu, which pauses the game
findings.code:
PinchState pinch = _pinch.Step(aimHand.IsTracked, aimHand.PinchStrength, pinchFireThreshold,
    pinchResetThreshold, false, 0f, Time.deltaTime);
findings.frequency: per-frame while the palm faces the user (system gesture armed)
findings.detail: Input is derived purely from joint distances. Nothing reads the Meta aim flags, although the installed XR Hands package exposes MetaAimFlags.SystemGesture (Library/PackageCache/com.unity.xr.hands@aec06f9cdb0b/Runtime/MetaAim.cs:75) and RS reports the Meta Hand Tracking Aim feature is enabled. WristMenu.cs:5-7 deliberately reuses the OS gesture (left palm to face plus pinch). When the right (aim) hand turns its palm toward the face and pinches, the Quest universal menu opens, OnApplicationFocus(false) fires, and MatchDirector.Pause runs (MatchDirector.cs:154-157), with no auto-resume. I have not verified on device how often this triggers mid-combat, so the impact is uncertain.
findings.fix: Read MetaAimHand.left/right aimFlags (Input System device) in HandGestureTracker. While SystemGesture is set, treat the pinch as not pressed and do not fire, and log the transition in PerfSpikeLogger. Add 'did the Meta menu or PAUSED appear?' to the device checklist.

findings.title: After a stall longer than 333 ms, palm-push speed is overestimated (clamped deltaTime against unscaled hand smoothing), which can fire a spurious shockwave right after a freeze
findings.code: float speed = Vector3.Dot(palmPosition - _lastPosition, palmNormal.normalized) / dt;
findings.frequency: per-frame (only matters on the first frame after a stall longer than 333 ms)
findings.detail: HandGestureTracker smooths palm positions with Time.unscaledDeltaTime (HandGestureTracker.cs:167), so after a long stall the smoothed palm jumps by almost all of the real displacement. XRHandsInputSource.SampleGestures passes dt = Time.deltaTime (XRHandsInputSource.cs:136), which is capped at 0.333 s, so the computed speed is real distance / 0.333 instead of real distance / stall length. With PushSpeed = 1.2 m/s (GestureRecognizers.cs:48), a 40 cm drift along the palm normal during a 1 s freeze reads as a push and fires a shockwave. This makes a freeze look worse, the same family of issue as BC-3. It is low-probability; I list it because none of the six auditors covered post-hitch input artifacts other than BC-3.
findings.fix: In the recognizer (or the input source), skip velocity-based gestures on frames where the unscaled frame time exceeds about 0.1 s: reset _lastPosition and return false. Add an EditMode test with a large-dt step.

critic.notes:
Coverage verdict: every game script that the built scene or the runtime prefabs reference was read by at least one auditor. I did a full script-GUID census of Arena_Main.unity: TextMeshPro x31, HandMenuButton x24, the HandProto scripts, XROrigin, TrackedPoseDriver, plus ARSession and ARCameraManager, both serialized m_Enabled: 0 and enabled only by ArenaViewMode in the MR table mode, which is selectable from the menu only. There are no XRI interactors, hand visualizers, EventSystem/Canvas (no class 223), Animator, ParticleSystem, Rigidbody, ReflectionProbe or MeshCollider. Core/ScriptedHandInputSource.cs, the one Core file nobody listed, is used only by ScriptedInputTests and has no runtime role. Legacy root scripts are not referenced (confirmed by the spawn auditor; my census agrees).

Freeze mechanisms from the checklist that I investigated and ruled out (evidence):
- Audio decompression or load: all three AudioSources (scene :5721, :9327; RunBot.prefab:415) have no clip, and fireSound is {fileID: 0} on the player, the Quick Match bot and RunBot, so PlayOneShot never runs.
- TMP dynamic atlas: all 31 TMP components use LiberationSans SDF (27 with a null font fall back to the TMP Settings default, guid 8f5863...). That asset is Static (m_AtlasPopulationMode: 0) and its 250-entry character table covers every printable ASCII code 32-126. Game and builder strings contain no non-ASCII literals; the only one is a Tooltip. The dynamic fallback is therefore never reached.
- Canvas rebuilds: there is no uGUI Canvas; all text is 3D TextMeshPro.
- Texture streaming: off on all quality levels.
- Realtime GI: off (m_EnableRealtimeLightmaps 0, builtin LightingDataAsset).
- Analytics, crash and performance reporting: all off (UnityConnectSettings).
- Optimized Frame Pacing: off.
- IL2CPP compiler configuration: default (Release).
- Builder wiring: execute.log has no field-wiring warnings, so no per-frame NullReference flood is expected from unwired fields.
- HandGestureTracker's only Debug.Log (line 141) fires once per change.
- HUD TMP rebuild frequency: RunHudText strings change at most about once per second or per HP change, because the clocks use CeilToInt and HP uses RoundToInt, and TMP's setter early-outs on equal strings. GM-1 is therefore an allocation cost, not a per-frame mesh rebuild.
- Shader/PSO: BeamImpact.mat is the only material used solely by a runtime-instantiated prefab. Any first-use cost happens once per session, so it cannot explain repeated random freezes.

Bug classes checked that nobody else listed:
- Divide-by-dt: only PalmPushRecognizer divides, and it is guarded for dt <= 0 (see CR-8 for the large-dt side).
- Re-entrancy: RunDirector's foreach over _bots is never re-entered from Died.
- RaycastNonAlloc truncation: the 16-slot buffer is unsorted, but the arena has about 10 active colliders during combat.
- Per-frame exceptions: none found.

Facts for PERF_REPORT:
- Package com.hyun.handhero (BuildScript.cs:21).
- persistentDataPath on Quest: /sdcard/Android/data/com.hyun.handhero/files, so the commands are `adb pull /sdcard/Android/data/com.hyun.handhero/files/perf_log.txt .` and `adb shell ls /sdcard/Android/data/com.hyun.handhero/files`. Hyun's PC: `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe" pull ...`.
- Incremental GC is already on (ProjectSettings.asset:925), so step 2's 'turn it on' needs no change.
- EditMode baseline: 321/321 passing (AUTO/logs/tests.xml, 2026-10-08 20:51Z).

Effort the gaps add to the auditors' estimate: CR-2/CR-3 logger design about 1.5-2 h (part of the planned logger work); CR-4 build script about 0.5 h; CR-5 setting change plus device check about 0.25 h; CR-6 Core pool model plus tests about 1-2 h; CR-1 tracking-lost cue about 0.5-1 h; CR-7/CR-8 about 1 h together. Most important for triage: before optimizing further, have Hyun answer whether the world itself stops (render stall, chase GC and spawn) or only his reticle and hero stop (tracking dropout, CR-1). Static evidence alone leaves both open, and the auditors' own notes say the measured allocation rates are unlikely to cause multi-hundred-ms freezes.
